1292: +
1293: +- The actor ID is the node's `<namespace>/<lab>/<node>` ID, the `container_id`
1294: +  inspect reports, and `actor_name` and `name` are the inspect `name`.
1295: +- `clab-node-name` is the node name as the topology spells it.
1296: +- `clab-topo-file` is the file the lab was deployed from (see
1297: +  [Topology file](#topology-file)).
1298: +- `state` is the container state after the event: `created`, `running` or
1299: +  `exited`. Docker leaves it to the client to derive it from the action; c9s
1300: +  reports it on every container event.
1301: +- `ports` lists the node's exposed ports without a host binding: they are
1302: +  reached through the node's Service or a port-forward, not on a port of the
1303: +  local machine.
1304: +- `kill` carries `signal` `15`; Kubernetes stops containers with SIGTERM.
1305: +- `create` can come before the controller has allocated the node's management
1306: +  address and Service, so it may lack `mgmt_ipv4`, `mgmt_ipv6` and `ports`;
1307: +  the following events carry them.
1308: +- `namespace`, `lab`, `node` and `pod` are c9s attributes on top.
1309: +
1310: +Docker attributes c9s does not report: `scope`, `clab-mgmt-net-bridge` (no
1311: +Docker bridge), `clab-node-lab-dir` (a c9s lab has no lab directory on the
1312: +deploying machine; node state lives in the cluster), and `exitCode` and
1313: +`execDuration` on `die`. `clab-node-type` and `clab-node-group` are reported
1314: +when the topology sets them, and with `-t` also a kind's default type; read by
1315: +`--name` alone, a default type such as SR Linux's `ixr-d2l` is not known.
1316:  
1317:  ### Interface events
1318:  
1319:  Containerlab samples the interfaces of every running node by exec into its
1320:  device container. One exec per node and interval reads `/proc/net/dev` and
1321:  `/sys/class/net/*/operstate` (with index, MTU, MAC address, flags and alias).
1322: -All containers of a device pod share one network namespace, so the samples
1323: -cover the node's pod interfaces.
1324:  
1325: -Interface state events are always streamed. They use the same schema as the
1326: -interface events of the local runtimes, with the operational state as action:
1327: +It reports the interfaces a Docker container of the same node kind has, named
1328: +as in that container:
1329: +
1330: +- the node's lab link interfaces, with the names and aliases clabwire lists for
1331: +  them (`containerlab capture --list`): `eth1` for a linux node, `e1-1` with
1332: +  alias `ethernet-1/1` for SR Linux, so a client finds a link's interface by
1333: +  the endpoint name in the topology or its alias
1334: +- the management interface `eth0`
1335: +- the loopback `lo`
1336: +
1337: +The pod's own interfaces (the pod network interface `c9s0`, clabernetes'
1338: +interposition interfaces `c9sr0` and `c9sm0`, and the link transport interfaces

88: // nodeExposedPorts reads the expose-port allocations the controller published on the Node.
89: func nodeExposedPorts(nodeResource *unstructured.Unstructured) []clablabruntime.ExposedPort {
90: 	rawPorts, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(
91: 		nodeResource.Object,
92: 		"status",
93: 		"exposedPorts",
94: 		"ports",
95: 	)
96: 
97: 	ports := make([]clablabruntime.ExposedPort, 0, len(rawPorts))
98: 	for _, raw := range rawPorts {
99: 		entry, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
100: 		if !ok {
101: 			continue
102: 		}
103: 
104: 		port := clablabruntime.ExposedPort{
105: 			Port:       intField(entry["destinationPort"]),
106: 			ExposePort: intField(entry["exposePort"]),
107: 			Protocol:   strings.ToLower(fmt.Sprint(entry["protocol"])),
108: 		}
109: 		if port.Port == 0 {
110: 			continue
111: 		}
112: 		if port.Protocol == "" || port.Protocol == "<nil>" {
113: 			port.Protocol = "tcp"
114: 		}
115: 
116: 		ports = append(ports, port)
117: 	}
118: 
119: 	if len(ports) == 0 {
120: 		return nil
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	sort.Slice(ports, func(i, j int) bool {
124: 		if ports[i].Port == ports[j].Port {
125: 			return ports[i].Protocol < ports[j].Protocol
126: 		}
127: 
128: 		return ports[i].Port < ports[j].Port
129: 	})
130: 
131: 	return ports
132: }

134: func intField(value any) int {
135: 	switch v := value.(type) {
136: 	case int64:
137: 		return int(v)
138: 	case int:
139: 		return v
140: 	case int32:
141: 		return int(v)
142: 	case float64:
143: 		return int(v)
144: 	default:
145: 		return 0
146: 	}
147: }

149: // newestPod prefers a pod that is not being deleted, then a running pod and, among equals, the
150: // newest one: several pods can match a node during a rolling update or a restart, when the old
151: // pod terminates while its replacement starts.
152: func newestPod(current, candidate *corev1.Pod) *corev1.Pod {
153: 	if current == nil {
154: 		return candidate
155: 	}
156: 
157: 	currentDeleting := current.DeletionTimestamp != nil
158: 	candidateDeleting := candidate.DeletionTimestamp != nil
159: 	if currentDeleting != candidateDeleting {
160: 		if candidateDeleting {
161: 			return current
162: 		}
163: 
164: 		return candidate
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	currentRunning := current.Status.Phase == corev1.PodRunning
168: 	candidateRunning := candidate.Status.Phase == corev1.PodRunning
169: 	if currentRunning != candidateRunning {
170: 		if candidateRunning {
171: 			return candidate
172: 		}
173: 
174: 		return current
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	if candidate.CreationTimestamp.After(current.CreationTimestamp.Time) {
178: 		return candidate
179: 	}
180: 
181: 	return current
182: }

184: func (r *Runtime) enrichState(ctx context.Context, state *clablabruntime.LabState) error {
185: 	if state == nil || state.Name == "" {
186: 		return nil
187: 	}
188: 
189: 	nodeResources, err := r.nodesForTopology(ctx, state.Name, state.Namespace)
190: 	if err != nil {
191: 		return err
192: 	}
193: 
194: 	nodesByName := map[string]clablabruntime.NodeState{}
195: 	for _, node := range state.Nodes {
196: 		nodesByName[node.Name] = node
197: 	}
198: 
199: 	networkModes := make(map[string]string, len(nodeResources.Items))
200: 	resourcesByName := make(map[string]*unstructured.Unstructured, len(nodeResources.Items))
201: 	for idx := range nodeResources.Items {
202: 		nodeResource := &nodeResources.Items[idx]
203: 		nodesByName[nodeResource.GetName()] = nodeStateFromResource(nodeResource)
204: 		networkModes[nodeResource.GetName()] = nodeNetworkMode(nodeResource)
205: 		resourcesByName[nodeResource.GetName()] = nodeResource
206: 	}
207: 
208: 	pods, err := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().Pods(state.Namespace).List(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{
209: 		LabelSelector: labels.Set{
210: 			labelApp:           clabernetesAppValue,
211: 			labelTopologyOwner: state.Name,
212: 		}.String(),
213: 	})
214: 	if err != nil {
215: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to list clabernetes pods for topology %s/%s: %w",
216: 			state.Namespace, state.Name, err)
217: 	}
218: 
219: 	podsByNode := map[string]*corev1.Pod{}
220: 	for idx := range pods.Items {
221: 		nodeName := pods.Items[idx].Labels[labelTopologyNode]
222: 		if nodeName == "" {
223: 			continue
224: 		}
225: 		// A pod of an earlier Node of the same name (a redeploy while the old pod still
226: 		// terminates) is not this node's pod.
227: 		if uid := pods.Items[idx].Annotations[annotationDirectNodeUID]; uid != "" {
228: 			if resource := resourcesByName[nodeName]; resource != nil &&
229: 				string(resource.GetUID()) != uid {
230: 				continue
231: 			}
232: 		}
233: 		podsByNode[nodeName] = newestPod(podsByNode[nodeName], &pods.Items[idx])
234: 	}
235: 
236: 	// The Node's status.readiness is the authoritative device signal. The primary Node's run
237: 	// state governs the pod a group of nodes shares: a stopped primary stops the whole group.
238: 	// Nodes without readiness yet report their pod phase.
239: 	for nodeName, node := range nodesByName {
240: 		primary := resolvePrimaryNode(nodeName, networkModes)
241: 		primaryResource := resourcesByName[primary]
242: 		stopRequested := primaryResource != nil &&
243: 			nodeRunState(primaryResource) == nodeRunStateStopped
244: 		if stopRequested {
245: 			node.State = "stopping"
246: 			if condition := nodeCondition(
247: 				primaryResource,
248: 				nodeConditionStopped,
249: 			); condition != nil &&
250: 				condition.status == string(metav1.ConditionTrue) {
251: 				node.State = "stopped"
252: 			}
253: 			node.Ready = false
254: 		} else if pod := podsByNode[primary]; node.State == "" && pod != nil &&
255: 			pod.Status.Phase != "" {
256: 			node.State = strings.ToLower(string(pod.Status.Phase))
257: 		}
258: 		node.ContainerState = nodeContainerState(stopRequested, podsByNode[primary])
259: 		if node.ContainerState == clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning {
260: 			node.Health = nodeHealth(node, resourcesByName[nodeName])
261: 		}
262: 		nodesByName[nodeName] = node
263: 	}
264: 
265: 	// Nodes grouped through network-mode container: share the pod of the group's primary
266: 	// node. Before the controller observed the device containers, the pod's default-container
267: 	// annotation names the primary node's container.
268: 	for nodeName, node := range nodesByName {
269: 		primary := resolvePrimaryNode(nodeName, networkModes)
270: 		pod := podsByNode[primary]
271: 		if pod == nil {
272: 			continue
273: 		}
274: 
275: 		node.Pod = pod.Name
276: 		if node.Container == "" && primary == nodeName {
277: 			node.Container = pod.Annotations[defaultContainerAnnotation]
278: 		}
279: 		nodesByName[nodeName] = node
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	nodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(nodesByName))
283: 	for nodeName := range nodesByName {
284: 		nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
285: 	}
286: 	sort.Strings(nodeNames)
287: 
288: 	state.Nodes = make([]clablabruntime.NodeState, 0, len(nodeNames))
289: 	allReady := len(nodeNames) > 0 // codespell:ignore allready
290: 	allStopped := len(nodeNames) > 0
291: 	for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
292: 		node := nodesByName[nodeName]
293: 		state.Nodes = append(state.Nodes, node)
294: 		allReady = allReady && node.Ready // codespell:ignore allready
295: 		allStopped = allStopped && node.State == "stopped"
296: 	}
297: 
298: 	switch {
299: 	case allReady: // codespell:ignore allready
300: 		state.State = "running"
301: 		state.Ready = true
302: 	case allStopped:
303: 		state.State = "stopped"
304: 		state.Ready = false
305: 	case len(nodeNames) != 0:
306: 		state.State = "partial"
307: 		state.Ready = false
308: 	}
309: 
310: 	return nil
311: }
312: 
313: // nodeContainerState is the state of a node in container runtime terms, from its pod: created
314: // while the pod is scheduled and prepared (init containers), running once the device containers
315: // run, and exited once the node was stopped, its pod is being deleted, or the pod ended. Between
316: // the pods of a restart the node is exited, then created.
317: func nodeContainerState(stopRequested bool, pod *corev1.Pod) string {
318: 	switch {
319: 	case pod == nil && stopRequested:
320: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited
321: 	case pod == nil:
322: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated
323: 	case stopRequested || pod.DeletionTimestamp != nil:
324: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited
325: 	}
326: 
327: 	switch pod.Status.Phase {
328: 	case corev1.PodRunning:
329: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning
330: 	case corev1.PodSucceeded, corev1.PodFailed:
331: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited
332: 	default:
333: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated
334: 	}
335: }
336: 
337: // nodeHealth is the health of a running node: healthy once the Node is ready or its device
338: // containers are, starting before. Device containers are the analogue of a container
339: // healthcheck: a node whose links wait for a stopped peer is not ready, but its device is.
340: func nodeHealth(node clablabruntime.NodeState, resource *unstructured.Unstructured) string {
341: 	if node.Ready {
342: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerHealthHealthy
343: 	}
344: 	if resource != nil {
345: 		if condition := nodeCondition(resource, nodeConditionContainersReady); condition != nil &&
346: 			condition.status == string(metav1.ConditionTrue) {
347: 			return clablabruntime.ContainerHealthHealthy
348: 		}
349: 	}
350: 
351: 	return clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting
352: }

5: package clabernetes
6: 
7: import (
8: 	"context"
9: 	"fmt"
10: 
11: 	clablabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime"

13: 	k8sruntime "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime"
14: )
15: 
16: // Manifests renders the resources a deploy would create for the topology, in the order the
17: // runtime applies them, without contacting the cluster. The bundle is the managed lab
18: // Namespace when containerlab would create one, the staged ConfigMaps every node file mounts
19: // from, and then either the Topology resource or, for a lab deployed without one, the
20: // NodeProfile, Link, and Node resources compiled client-side. Every object carries the labels
21: // the runtime relies on to discover the lab later, so a bundle applied by hand stays
22: // manageable with inspect, destroy, and the node lifecycle commands.
23: func (r *Runtime) Manifests(
24: 	ctx context.Context,
25: 	req clablabruntime.DeployRequest,
26: ) ([]clablabruntime.Manifest, error) {
27: 	if req.Name == "" {
28: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("topology name is required")
29: 	}
30: 	if len(req.TopologyDefinition) == 0 {
31: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("rendered containerlab topology is required")
32: 	}
33: 
34: 	namespace, err := r.namespaceForLab(req.Name, req.Namespace)
35: 	if err != nil {
36: 		return nil, err
37: 	}
38: 	prepared, err := prepareDesiredDeployment(ctx, req, namespace)
39: 	if err != nil {
40: 		return nil, err
41: 	}
42: 
43: 	// The manifests are applied by other means than this deploy, so they do not carry the path
44: 	// of the topology file on this machine; such a lab reports where its definition lives.
45: 	removeTopologySourceFile(prepared.topology)
46: 	for _, group := range prepared.primitives.groups() {
47: 		for _, obj := range group.objects {
48: 			removeTopologySourceFile(obj)
49: 		}
50: 	}
51: 
52: 	manifests := []clablabruntime.Manifest{}
53: 
54: 	// A namespace override must already exist, matching the deploy contract; only the
55: 	// canonical per-lab namespace is created by containerlab and therefore emitted.
56: 	if req.Namespace == "" && r.labNamespaceOverride == "" {
57: 		manifest, err := typedManifest(labNamespaceObject(req.Name, namespace))
58: 		if err != nil {
59: 			return nil, err
60: 		}
61: 		manifests = append(manifests, manifest)
62: 	}
63: 
64: 	for _, staged := range prepared.configMaps {
65: 		manifest, err := typedManifest(stagedConfigMapObject(namespace, req.Name, staged, nil))
66: 		if err != nil {
67: 			return nil, err
68: 		}
69: 		manifests = append(manifests, manifest)
70: 	}
71: 
72: 	if !req.NoTopologyCR {
73: 		return append(manifests, unstructuredManifest(prepared.topology)), nil
74: 	}
75: 
76: 	for _, group := range prepared.primitives.groups() {
77: 		for _, obj := range group.objects {
78: 			manifests = append(manifests, unstructuredManifest(obj))
79: 		}
80: 	}
81: 
82: 	return manifests, nil
83: }
84: 
85: func typedManifest(obj k8sruntime.Object) (clablabruntime.Manifest, error) {
86: 	object, err := k8sruntime.DefaultUnstructuredConverter.ToUnstructured(obj)
87: 	if err != nil {
88: 		return clablabruntime.Manifest{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to render manifest: %w", err)
89: 	}
90: 
91: 	return unstructuredManifest(&unstructured.Unstructured{Object: object}), nil
92: }
93: 
94: // unstructuredManifest copies the object and strips the server-populated fields that typed
95: // conversion materializes as empty values, so the emitted document is a clean input for apply.
96: func unstructuredManifest(obj *unstructured.Unstructured) clablabruntime.Manifest {
97: 	object := obj.DeepCopy().Object
98: 
99: 	unstructured.RemoveNestedField(object, "status")
100: 	if timestamp, found, _ := unstructured.NestedFieldNoCopy(
101: 		object, "metadata", "creationTimestamp",
102: 	); found && timestamp == nil {
103: 		unstructured.RemoveNestedField(object, "metadata", "creationTimestamp")
104: 	}
105: 	if spec, found, _ := unstructured.NestedMap(object, "spec"); found && len(spec) == 0 {
106: 		unstructured.RemoveNestedField(object, "spec")
107: 	}
108: 
109: 	copied := &unstructured.Unstructured{Object: object}
110: 
111: 	return clablabruntime.Manifest{
112: 		APIVersion: copied.GetAPIVersion(),
113: 		Kind:       copied.GetKind(),
114: 		Namespace:  copied.GetNamespace(),
115: 		Name:       copied.GetName(),
116: 		Object:     object,
117: 	}
118: }

found && timestamp == nil {\n\t\tunstructured.RemoveNestedField(object, \"metadata\", \"creationTimestamp\")\n\t}\n\tif spec, found, _ := unstructured.NestedMap(object, \"spec\"); found && len(spec) == 0 {\n\t\tunstructured.RemoveNestedField(object, \"spec\")\n\t}\n\n\tcopied := &unstructured.Unstructured{Object: object}\n\n\treturn clablabruntime.Manifest{\n\t\tAPIVersion: copied.GetAPIVersion(),\n\t\tKind:       copied.GetKind(),\n\t\tNamespace:  copied.GetNamespace(),\n\t\tName:       copied.GetName(),\n\t\tObject:     object,\n\t}\n}",

1: package clabernetes

3: import (

21: // streamPodExec runs a command in a pod container without a terminal and streams its stdout
22: // and stderr. A non-nil stdin is attached: when it ends, the process's stdin is closed (the
23: // websocket v5 close signal, or a half-closed SPDY stream). A nonzero exit returns a
24: // *labruntime.CommandExitError.
25: func (r *Runtime) streamPodExec(
26: 	ctx context.Context,
27: 	namespace, pod, container string,
28: 	command []string,
29: 	stdin io.Reader,
30: 	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
31: ) error {
32: 	execURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().
33: 		Resource("pods").
34: 		Name(pod).
35: 		Namespace(namespace).
36: 		SubResource("exec").
37: 		VersionedParams(&corev1.PodExecOptions{
38: 			Container: container,
39: 			Command:   command,
40: 			Stdin:     stdin != nil,
41: 			Stdout:    stdout != nil,
42: 			Stderr:    stderr != nil,
43: 		}, scheme.ParameterCodec).URL()
44: 
45: 	executor, err := r.newExecutor(execURL)
46: 	if err != nil {
47: 		return err
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	// client-go reports streams cut by a cancelled context through the context's logger; a
51: 	// capture ends that way on purpose, so it goes to the debug log
52: 	err = executor.StreamWithContext(withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx),
53: 		remotecommand.StreamOptions{
54: 			Stdin:  stdin,
55: 			Stdout: stdout,
56: 			Stderr: stderr,
57: 		})
58: 
59: 	var exitErr kubeexec.ExitError
60: 	if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
61: 		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: exitErr.ExitStatus()}
62: 	}
63: 	if err != nil {
64: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to execute command in pod %s/%s container %s: %w",
65: 			namespace, pod, container, err)
66: 	}
67: 
68: 	return nil
69: }
70: 
71: // InspectInterfaces lists the interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every running node, in
72: // the shape of `inspect interfaces`, with the interfaces the interface events report: the lab
73: // link interfaces and their aliases as clabwire lists them, the management interface and
74: // loopback. Per node (named <lab>-<node> like in inspect) it reports the MAC address, index,
75: // MTU and operational state read from sysfs in the device container. A node whose device
76: // container has no shell reports its link interfaces without these attributes.
77: func (r *Runtime) InspectInterfaces(
78: 	ctx context.Context,
79: 	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
80: ) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error) {
81: 	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
82: 	if err != nil {
83: 		return nil, err
84: 	}
85: 
86: 	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
87: 		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: req.Nodes, Identity: req.Identity,
88: 	})
89: 	if err != nil {
90: 		return nil, err
91: 	}
92: 
93: 	running := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(locations))
94: 	for _, location := range locations {
95: 		if location.Pod == "" {
96: 			log.Warn("Skipping interface detection of a node that does not run",
97: 				"node", location.NodeName)
98: 			continue
99: 		}
100: 		running = append(running, location)
101: 	}
102: 
103: 	listed, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, running)
104: 	if err != nil {
105: 		return nil, err
106: 	}
107: 	states := r.sampleInterfaceStates(ctx, running)
108: 
109: 	result := make([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, 0, len(running))
110: 	for _, location := range running {
111: 		container := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces{
112: 			ContainerName: req.Name + "-" + location.NodeName,
113: 			Interfaces:    []*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{},
114: 		}
115: 		sampled, hasStates := states[location.NodeName]
116: 		for name, alias := range reportedInterfaces(listed[location.NodeName]) {
117: 			state, ok := sampled[name]
118: 			if !ok {
119: 				if hasStates || (name == managementInterface || name == loopbackInterface) {
120: 					// not present in the node (yet), or not known without its states
121: 					continue
122: 				}
123: 				state = c9sIfaceState{Name: name}
124: 			}
125: 
126: 			data := interfaceEventData(state, alias)
127: 			details := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{
128: 				InterfaceName:  data.Name,
129: 				InterfaceAlias: data.Alias,
130: 				InterfaceType:  data.Type,
131: 				InterfaceMAC:   data.MAC,
132: 				InterfaceIndex: data.Index,
133: 				InterfaceMTU:   data.MTU,
134: 			}
135: 			if ok {
136: 				details.InterfaceState = data.OperState
137: 			}
138: 			container.Interfaces = append(container.Interfaces, details)
139: 		}
140: 		sort.Slice(container.Interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
141: 			return container.Interfaces[i].InterfaceName < container.Interfaces[j].InterfaceName
142: 		})
143: 		result = append(result, container)
144: 	}
145: 	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {
146: 		return result[i].ContainerName < result[j].ContainerName
147: 	})
148: 
149: 	return result, nil
150: }
151: 
152: // sampleInterfaceStates reads the sysfs interface attributes of every node's device container,
153: // one exec per node, with the script the interface events use.
154: func (r *Runtime) sampleInterfaceStates(
155: 	ctx context.Context,
156: 	locations []clablabruntime.NodeLocation,
157: ) map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState {
158: 	var mu sync.Mutex
159: 	result := map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState{}
160: 
161: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
162: 	workers := make(chan struct{}, interfaceSampleWorkers)
163: 	exec := r.execInPodContainer()
164: 	for _, location := range locations {
165: 		wg.Add(1)
166: 		go func() {
167: 			defer wg.Done()
168: 			workers <- struct{}{}
169: 			defer func() { <-workers }()
170: 
171: 			var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
172: 			err := exec(ctx, location.Namespace, location.Pod, location.Container,
173: 				[]string{"sh", "-c", interfaceSampleScript}, nil, &stdout, &stderr)
174: 			if err != nil {
175: 				log.Debug("Cannot read the interface state of a c9s node",
176: 					"node", location.NodeName, "error", err)
177: 				return
178: 			}
179: 			_, ifaces, _, err := parseInterfaceSample(stdout.Bytes())
180: 			if err != nil {
181: 				log.Debug("Cannot parse the interface state of a c9s node",
182: 					"node", location.NodeName, "error", err)
183: 				return
184: 			}
185: 
186: 			byName := make(map[string]c9sIfaceState, len(ifaces))
187: 			for _, iface := range ifaces {
188: 				byName[iface.Name] = iface
189: 			}
190: 			mu.Lock()
191: 			result[location.NodeName] = byName
192: 			mu.Unlock()
193: 		}()
194: 	}
195: 	wg.Wait()
196: 
197: 	return result
198: }

A nonzero exit returns a\n// *labruntime.CommandExitError.\nfunc (r *Runtime) streamPodExec(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tnamespace, pod, container string,\n\tcommand []string,\n\tstdin io.Reader,\n\tstdout, stderr io.Writer,\n) error {\n\texecURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().\n\t\tResource(\"pods\").\n\t\tName(pod).\n\t\tNamespace(namespace).\n\t\tSubResource(\"exec\").\n\t\tVersionedParams(&corev1.PodExecOptions{\n\t\t\tContainer: container,\n\t\t\tCommand:   command,\n\t\t\tStdin:     stdin != nil,\n\t\t\tStdout:    stdout != nil,\n\t\t\tStderr:    stderr != nil,\n\t\t}, scheme.ParameterCodec).URL()\n\n\texecutor, err := r.newExecutor(execURL)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// client-go reports streams cut by a cancelled context through the context's logger; a\n\t// capture ends that way on purpose, so it goes to the debug log\n\terr = executor.StreamWithContext(withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx),\n\t\tremotecommand.StreamOptions{\n\t\t\tStdin:  stdin,\n\t\t\tStdout: stdout,\n\t\t\tStderr: stderr,\n\t\t})\n\n\tvar exitErr kubeexec.ExitError\n\tif errors.As(err, &exitErr) {\n\t\treturn &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: exitErr.ExitStatus()}\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to execute command in pod %s/%s container %s: %w\",\n\t\t\tnamespace, pod, container, err)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// InspectInterfaces lists the interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every running node, in\n// the shape of `inspect interfaces`, with the interfaces the interface events report: the lab\n// link interfaces and their aliases as clabwire lists them, the management interface and\n// loopback. Per node (named <lab>-<node> like in inspect) it reports the MAC address, index,\n// MTU and operational state read from sysfs in the device container. A node whose device\n// container has no shell reports its link interfaces without these attributes.\nfunc (r *Runtime) InspectInterfaces(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\treq clablabruntime.NodeRequest,\n) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error) {\n\tr, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tlocations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{\n\t\tName: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: req.Nodes, Identity: req.Identity,\n\t})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\trunning := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(locations))\n\tfor _, location := range locations {\n\t\tif location.Pod == \"\" {\n\t\t\tlog.Warn(\"Skipping interface detection of a node that does not run\",\n\t\t\t\t\"node\", location.NodeName)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\trunning = append(running, location)\n\t}\n\n\tlisted, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, running)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tstates := r.sampleInterfaceStates(ctx, running)\n\n\tresult := make([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, 0, len(running))\n\tfor _, location := range running {\n\t\tcontainer := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces{\n\t\t\tContainerName: req.Name + \"-\" + location.NodeName,\n\t\t\tInterfaces:    []*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{},\n\t\t}\n\t\tsampled, hasStates := states[location.NodeName]\n\t\tfor name, alias := range reportedInterfaces(listed[location.NodeName]) {\n\t\t\tstate, ok := sampled[name]\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\tif hasStates || (name == managementInterface || name == loopbackInterface) {\n\t\t\t\t\t// not present in the node (yet), or not known without its states\n\t\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tstate = c9sIfaceState{Name: name}\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tdata := interfaceEventData(state, alias)\n\t\t\tdetails := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{\n\t\t\t\tInterfaceName:  data.Name,\n\t\t\t\tInterfaceAlias: data.Alias,\n\t\t\t\tInterfaceType:  data.Type,\n\t\t\t\tInterfaceMAC:   data.MAC,\n\t\t\t\tInterfaceIndex: data.Index,\n\t\t\t\tInterfaceMTU:   data.MTU,\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif ok {\n\t\t\t\tdetails.InterfaceState = data.OperState\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontainer.Interfaces = append(container.Interfaces, details)\n\t\t}\n\t\tsort.Slice(container.Interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\t\treturn container.Interfaces[i].InterfaceName < container.Interfaces[j].InterfaceName\n\t\t})\n\t\tresult = append(result, container)\n\t}\n\tsort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\treturn result[i].ContainerName < result[j].ContainerName\n\t})\n\n\treturn result, nil\n}\n\n// sampleInterfaceStates reads the sysfs interface attributes of every node's device container,\n// one exec per node, with the script the interface events use.\nfunc (r *Runtime) sampleInterfaceStates(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tlocations []clablabruntime.NodeLocation,\n) map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState {\n\tvar mu sync.Mutex\n\tresult := map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState{}\n\n\tvar wg sync.WaitGroup\n\tworkers := make(chan struct{}, interfaceSampleWorkers)\n\texec := r.execInPodContainer()\n\tfor _, location := range locations {\n\t\twg.Add(1)\n\t\tgo func() {\n\t\t\tdefer wg.Done()\n\t\t\tworkers <- struct{}{}\n\t\t\tdefer func() { <-workers }()\n\n\t\t\tvar stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer\n\t\t\terr := exec(ctx, location.Namespace, location.Pod, location.Container,\n\t\t\t\t[]string{\"sh\", \"-c\", interfaceSampleScript}, {\n\t\t\t\tbyName[iface.Name] = iface\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tmu.Lock()\n\t\t\tresult[location.NodeName] = byName\n\t\t\tmu.Unlock()\n\t\t}()\n\t}\n\twg.Wait()\n\n\treturn result\n}",

1: package clabernetes

3: import (

15: type topologyObjectOption func(map[string]any)
16: 
17: // annotationTopologyFile records the absolute path of the topology file a lab was deployed from,
18: // on the machine that deployed it. Inspect reports it as the lab's topology path and events as
19: // clab-topo-file, as the local runtimes do, so clients match the running lab to its file. A lab
20: // created by other means than a containerlab deploy has no annotation and reports where its
21: // definition lives in the cluster (k8s://<namespace>/topologies/<lab>).
22: const annotationTopologyFile = "containerlab.dev/topo-file"
23: 
24: // setTopologySourceFile records the topology file a deploy reads on the Topology. An empty path
25: // (a definition that came from no file) records nothing.
26: func setTopologySourceFile(topology *unstructured.Unstructured, path string) {
27: 	if path == "" {
28: 		return
29: 	}
30: 
31: 	annotations := topology.GetAnnotations()
32: 	if annotations == nil {
33: 		annotations = map[string]string{}
34: 	}
35: 	annotations[annotationTopologyFile] = path
36: 	topology.SetAnnotations(annotations)
37: }
38: 
39: // removeTopologySourceFile drops the deploying machine's file path from an object.
40: func removeTopologySourceFile(obj *unstructured.Unstructured) {
41: 	annotations := obj.GetAnnotations()
42: 	if _, ok := annotations[annotationTopologyFile]; !ok {
43: 		return
44: 	}
45: 
46: 	delete(annotations, annotationTopologyFile)
47: 	if len(annotations) == 0 {
48: 		annotations = nil
49: 	}
50: 	obj.SetAnnotations(annotations)
51: }
52: 
53: // labTopologyPath is the topology path a lab reports: the file it was deployed from when the
54: // deploy recorded one, otherwise the place given.
55: func labTopologyPath(annotations map[string]string, fallback string) string {
56: 	if path := annotations[annotationTopologyFile]; path != "" {
57: 		return path
58: 	}
59: 
60: 	return fallback
61: }
62: 
63: func topologyWithNaming(naming string) topologyObjectOption {
64: 	return func(spec map[string]any) {
65: 		if naming != "" {
66: 			spec["naming"] = naming
67: 		}
68: 	}
69: }
70: 
71: // topologyWithImagePullSecret sets the image pull secret the kubelet uses when pulling device
72: // images. An empty name leaves imagePull unset entirely: the controller fails closed on a named
73: // Secret that does not exist, so a Topology must only reference one the deploy actually asked
74: // for.
75: func topologyWithImagePullSecret(secret string) topologyObjectOption {
76: 	return func(spec map[string]any) {
77: 		if secret == "" {
78: 			return
79: 		}
80: 		spec["imagePull"] = map[string]any{
81: 			"pullSecrets": []any{secret},
82: 		}
83: 	}
84: }
85: 
86: func topologyWithExposeType(exposeType string) topologyObjectOption {
87: 	return func(spec map[string]any) {
88: 		if exposeType == "" {
89: 			return
90: 		}
91: 		spec["expose"] = map[string]any{
92: 			"exposeType": exposeType,
93: 		}
94: 	}
95: }
96: 
97: // topologyWithPersistence backs each node's artifact volume with a persistent claim so saved
98: // device configuration survives Pod replacement, the same contract a local runtime provides
99: // through the lab directory. The claims are retained when their Node is deleted, so a plain
100: // destroy keeps the saved configuration like the local lab directory, and a redeploy boots from
101: // it; destroy --cleanup deletes them. Disabled leaves persistence unset entirely: ephemeral
102: // storage is the CRD default.
103: func topologyWithPersistence(enabled bool) topologyObjectOption {
104: 	return func(spec map[string]any) {
105: 		if !enabled {
106: 			return
107: 		}
108: 		deployment, ok := spec["deployment"].(map[string]any)
109: 		if !ok {
110: 			deployment = map[string]any{}
111: 			spec["deployment"] = deployment
112: 		}
113: 		deployment["persistence"] = map[string]any{
114: 			"enabled": true,
115: 			"reclaim": persistenceReclaimRetain,
116: 		}
117: 	}
118: }
119: 
120: func topologyObject(
121: 	name,
122: 	namespace,
123: 	owner,
124: 	definition string,
125: 	opts ...topologyObjectOption,
126: ) *unstructured.Unstructured {
127: 	topologyLabels := map[string]any{
128: 		"containerlab.dev/runtime": clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName,
129: 	}
130: 	topologyAnnotations := map[string]any{}
131: 	if owner != "" {
132: 		topologyAnnotations[clabconstants.Owner] = owner
133: 		if len(validation.IsValidLabelValue(owner)) == 0 {
134: 			topologyLabels[clabconstants.Owner] = owner
135: 		}
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	metadata := map[string]any{
139: 		"name":      name,
140: 		"namespace": namespace,
141: 		"labels":    topologyLabels,
142: 	}
143: 	if len(topologyAnnotations) != 0 {
144: 		metadata["annotations"] = topologyAnnotations
145: 	}
146: 
147: 	spec := map[string]any{
148: 		"definition": map[string]any{
149: 			"containerlab": definition,
150: 		},
151: 		// The runtime's readiness contract requires c9s status probes. Persist the setting
152: 		// explicitly: CRD defaulting cannot materialize it in an absent statusProbes object, and
153: 		// the controller's typed writes would then pin the zero value (disabled) instead. This
154: 		// mirrors configurePrimitiveReadiness on the client-side compile.
155: 		"statusProbes": map[string]any{
156: 			"enabled": true,
157: 		},
158: 	}
159: 	for _, opt := range opts {
160: 		opt(spec)
161: 	}
162: 
163: 	return &unstructured.Unstructured{
164: 		Object: map[string]any{
165: 			"apiVersion": c9sAPIVersion,
166: 			"kind":       "Topology",
167: 			"metadata":   metadata,
168: 			"spec":       spec,
169: 		},
170: 	}
171: }
172: 
173: // stateFromTopology builds the lab-state skeleton from a Topology CR. The direct-runtime
174: // Topology status intentionally carries only aggregate readiness -- per-node detail is always
175: // filled in from the Node objects and workloads by enrichState.
176: func stateFromTopology(obj *unstructured.Unstructured, namespace string) *clablabruntime.LabState {
177: 	if obj.GetNamespace() != "" {
178: 		namespace = obj.GetNamespace()
179: 	}
180: 
181: 	ready, _, _ := unstructured.NestedBool(obj.Object, "status", "topologyReady")
182: 	state, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(obj.Object, "status", "topologyState")
183: 	owner := obj.GetLabels()[clabconstants.Owner]
184: 	if owner == "" {
185: 		owner = obj.GetAnnotations()[clabconstants.Owner]
186: 	}
187: 	nodeSpecs := nodeSpecsFromTopology(obj)
188: 	topologyPath := labTopologyPath(
189: 		obj.GetAnnotations(),
190: 		fmt.Sprintf("k8s://%s/topologies/%s", namespace, obj.GetName()),
191: 	)
192: 
193: 	nodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(nodeSpecs))
194: 	for nodeName := range nodeSpecs {
195: 		nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
196: 	}
197: 	sort.Strings(nodeNames)
198: 
199: 	nodes := make([]clablabruntime.NodeState, 0, len(nodeNames))
200: 	for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
201: 		spec := nodeSpecs[nodeName]
202: 		nodes = append(nodes, clablabruntime.NodeState{
203: 			Name:  nodeName,
204: 			Kind:  spec.Kind,
205: 			Image: spec.Image,
206: 		})
207: 	}
208: 
209: 	return &clablabruntime.LabState{
210: 		Name:         obj.GetName(),
211: 		Namespace:    namespace,
212: 		Owner:        owner,
213: 		TopologyPath: topologyPath,
214: 		State:        state,
215: 		Ready:        ready,
216: 		Nodes:        nodes,
217: 	}
218: }
219: 
220: type nodeSpec struct {
221: 	Kind  string `yaml:"kind"`
222: 	Image string `yaml:"image"`
223: }
224: 
225: type containerlabDefinition struct {
226: 	Topology struct {
227: 		Nodes map[string]nodeSpec `yaml:"nodes"`
228: 	} `yaml:"topology"`
229: }
230: 
231: func nodeSpecsFromTopology(obj *unstructured.Unstructured) map[string]nodeSpec {
232: 	specs := map[string]nodeSpec{}
233: 
234: 	definition, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(
235: 		obj.Object,
236: 		"spec",
237: 		"definition",
238: 		"containerlab",
239: 	)
240: 	mergeNodeSpecs(specs, definition)
241: 
242: 	return specs
243: }
244: 
245: func mergeNodeSpecs(specs map[string]nodeSpec, definition string) {
246: 	if definition == "" {
247: 		return
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	var parsed containerlabDefinition
251: 	if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(definition), &parsed); err != nil {
252: 		log.Debug("failed to parse C9s topology definition", "error", err)
253: 		return
254: 	}
255: 
256: 	for nodeName, spec := range parsed.Topology.Nodes {
257: 		specs[nodeName] = spec
258: 	}
259: }

114: type clientLoader struct {

116: 	newClients func(*rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error)

134: func newKubeClients(restConfig *rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error) {
135: 	client, err := dynamic.NewForConfig(restConfig)
136: 	if err != nil {
137: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes dynamic client: %w", err)
138: 	}
139: 
140: 	kubeClient, err := kubernetes.NewForConfig(restConfig)
141: 	if err != nil {
142: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes client: %w", err)
143: 	}
144: 
145: 	return &kubeClients{dynamic: client, kube: kubeClient, restConfig: restConfig}, nil
146: }

148: // load returns the clients of an identity. The impersonation is part of the rest config, so it
149: // applies to every transport built from it: REST calls, watches, log streams, and the SPDY and
150: // websocket upgrades of exec, attach and port-forward.
151: func (l *clientLoader) load(
152: 	identity clablabruntime.Identity,
153: ) (*kubeClients, string, error) {
154: 	l.once.Do(func() {
155: 		l.base, l.namespace, l.err = l.loadConfig()
156: 		if l.namespace == "" {
157: 			l.namespace = defaultNamespace
158: 		}
159: 	})
160: 	if l.err != nil {
161: 		return nil, "", l.err
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	key := identityKey(identity)
165: 
166: 	l.mu.Lock()
167: 	defer l.mu.Unlock()
168: 
169: 	if clients, ok := l.byIdentity[key]; ok {
170: 		return clients, l.namespace, nil
171: 	}
172: 
173: 	restConfig := rest.CopyConfig(l.base)
174: 	if !identity.IsZero() {
175: 		restConfig.Impersonate = rest.ImpersonationConfig{
176: 			UserName: identity.User,
177: 			Groups:   slices.Clone(identity.Groups),
178: 		}
179: 	}
180: 
181: 	clients, err := l.newClients(restConfig)
182: 	if err != nil {
183: 		return nil, "", err
184: 	}
185: 	if l.byIdentity == nil {
186: 		l.byIdentity = map[string]*kubeClients{}
187: 	}
188: 	l.byIdentity[key] = clients
189: 
190: 	return clients, l.namespace, nil
191: }

193: func identityKey(identity clablabruntime.Identity) string {
194: 	return identity.User + "\x00" + strings.Join(identity.Groups, "\x00")
195: }

197: // connect returns a view of the runtime with the Kubernetes clients of an identity populated,
198: // loading the kubeconfig on first use. A zero identity uses the runtime's configured identity.
199: // Every operation that reads or changes cluster state calls it first, so it also runs the
200: // clabernetes version check once per runtime instance, before the first cluster call.
201: func (r *Runtime) connect(
202: 	ctx context.Context,
203: 	identity clablabruntime.Identity,
204: ) (*Runtime, error) {
205: 	if identity.IsZero() {
206: 		identity = r.identity
207: 	}
208: 	if r.connected && identity.Equal(r.identity) {
209: 		return r, nil
210: 	}
211: 	if r.clients == nil {
212: 		// clients were injected (tests); they act as the identity they were built with
213: 		if err := r.support.ensure(ctx, r); err != nil {
214: 			return nil, err
215: 		}
216: 
217: 		return r, nil
218: 	}
219: 
220: 	clients, namespace, err := r.clients.load(identity)
221: 	if err != nil {
222: 		return nil, err
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	view := *r
226: 	view.client = clients.dynamic
227: 	view.kubeClient = clients.kube
228: 	view.restConfig = clients.restConfig
229: 	if view.namespace == "" {
230: 		view.namespace = namespace
231: 	}
232: 	view.identity = identity
233: 	view.connected = true
234: 
235: 	if err := r.support.ensure(ctx, &view); err != nil {
236: 		return nil, err
237: 	}
238: 
239: 	return &view, nil
240: }

248: 		log.Debug("Kubernetes client", "log", strings.TrimSpace(prefix+" "+args))
249: 	}, funcr.Options{Verbosity: verbosity})
250: 
251: 	return klog.NewContext(ctx, logger)
252: }

354: // resolveCaptureTargets locates every target node, checks every interface against the
355: // interfaces clabwire allows, and groups the targets per node.
356: func (r *Runtime) resolveCaptureTargets(
357: 	ctx context.Context,
358: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
359: ) (*resolvedCapture, error) {
360: 	nodeOrder := make([]string, 0, len(req.Targets))
361: 	seenNodes := map[string]bool{}
362: 	for _, target := range req.Targets {
363: 		if !seenNodes[target.Node] {
364: 			seenNodes[target.Node] = true
365: 			nodeOrder = append(nodeOrder, target.Node)
366: 		}
367: 	}
368: 
369: 	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
370: 		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: nodeOrder, Identity: req.Identity,
371: 	})
372: 	if err != nil {
373: 		return nil, err
374: 	}
375: 	byRequest := make(map[string]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, len(nodeOrder))
376: 	for idx, name := range nodeOrder {
377: 		byRequest[name] = locations[idx]
378: 	}
379: 
380: 	listed, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, locations)
381: 	if err != nil {
382: 		return nil, err
383: 	}
384: 	names, err := r.nodeDisplayNames(ctx, req.Name, locations)
385: 	if err != nil {
386: 		return nil, err
387: 	}
388: 
389: 	resolved := &resolvedCapture{}
390: 	groups := map[string]*captureGroup{}
391: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
392: 	for _, target := range req.Targets {
393: 		location := byRequest[target.Node]
394: 		entry, ok := findCaptureInterface(listed[location.NodeName], target.Interface)
395: 		if !ok {
396: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is not a capturable link "+
397: 				"interface; capturable: %s", target.Interface, target.Node,
398: 				describeCaptureInterfaces(listed[location.NodeName]))
399: 		}
400: 
401: 		key := location.NodeName + "\x00" + entry.Interface
402: 		if seen[key] {
403: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is requested more than once",
404: 				entry.Interface, target.Node)
405: 		}
406: 		seen[key] = true
407: 
408: 		group := groups[location.NodeName]
409: 		if group == nil {
410: 			group = &captureGroup{
411: 				location: location,
412: 				display:  names.display(location.NodeName),
413: 			}
414: 			groups[location.NodeName] = group
415: 			resolved.groups = append(resolved.groups, group)
416: 		}
417: 
418: 		id := uint32(len(resolved.names)) //nolint:gosec // bounded by the targets
419: 		group.interfaces = append(group.interfaces, entry.Interface)
420: 		group.ids = append(group.ids, id)
421: 		resolved.names = append(resolved.names, group.display+":"+entry.Interface)
422: 	}
423: 
424: 	return resolved, nil
425: }

443: func describeCaptureInterfaces(entries []clabwireInterface) string {
444: 	if len(entries) == 0 {

446: 	}

448: 	names := make([]string, 0, len(entries))
449: 	for _, entry := range entries {

451: 		if entry.Alias != "" {
452: 			name += " (" + entry.Alias + ")"
453: 		}

460: // Capture streams pcapng from lab link interfaces to w: one section, one Interface Description
461: // Block per target in request order named <node>:<interface>, then the packets of every target.
462: //
463: // Each node's interfaces are captured by one clabwire process in the node's pod. clabwire limits
464: // a capture to one hour, so a longer capture (or one without Duration) chains captures: the next
465: // one starts before the current one ends, and the stream switches at a cut in the overlap. See
466: // captureChain for how packets of the overlap are kept once.
467: //
468: // Packets go out in timestamp order across nodes, through a reorder buffer (captureReorder).
469: //
470: // Every clabwire process runs with stdin attached and --stop-on-stdin-close: a Kubernetes exec
471: // does not stop its process when the stream closes, so containerlab closes stdin whenever a
472: // segment ends (the capture ends, fails, its output fails, or a newer segment took over) and
473: // clabwire ends the capture itself.
474: //
475: // Capture returns when Duration has passed, PacketLimit packets were written, or ctx ends; an
476: // ended ctx is not an error. Every block reaches w in one write, so the stream is a valid capture
477: // whenever it stops. A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error.
478: func (r *Runtime) Capture(
479: 	ctx context.Context,
480: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
481: 	w io.Writer,
482: ) error {
483: 	if err := clabcapture.ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {
484: 		return err
485: 	}
486: 
487: 	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
488: 	if err != nil {
489: 		return err
490: 	}
491: 
492: 	resolved, err := r.resolveCaptureTargets(ctx, req)
493: 	if err != nil {
494: 		return err
495: 	}
496: 
497: 	captureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)
498: 	defer stop()
499: 
500: 	out, err := clabcapture.NewOutput(w, resolved.names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit,
501: 		r.captureReorderWindowLength(), stop)
502: 	if err != nil {
503: 		return err
504: 	}
505: 
506: 	run := &captureRun{
507: 		r:       r,
508: 		req:     req,
509: 		out:     out,
510: 		segment: r.captureSegmentLength(),
511: 	}
512: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
513: 		run.deadline = time.Now().Add(req.Duration)
514: 	}
515: 	run.overlap = min(maxCaptureOverlap, run.segment/3)
516: 	run.window = min(maxCaptureCutWindow, run.overlap/4)
517: 
518: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
519: 		// a clabwire process that does not end on its own does not hold the capture open
520: 		var cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc
521: 		captureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx,
522: 			req.Duration+run.overlap+captureEndGrace)
523: 		defer cancelTimeout()
524: 	}
525: 
526: 	group, groupCtx := errgroup.WithContext(captureCtx)
527: 	for _, captureGroup := range resolved.groups {
528: 		chain := &captureChain{capture: run, group: captureGroup}
529: 		group.Go(func() error {
530: 			return chain.run(groupCtx)
531: 		})
532: 	}
533: 
534: 	err = group.Wait()
535: 	if writeErr := out.Close(); writeErr != nil {
536: 		return writeErr
537: 	}
538: 	if err != nil && !(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && captureCtx.Err() != nil) {
539: 		return err
540: 	}
541: 
542: 	return nil
543: }

545: // captureRun is the state a capture's chains share.
546: type captureRun struct {
547: 	r   *Runtime
548: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest
549: 	// out is the merged stream; it writes the packets of every chain in timestamp order and
550: 	// stops every chain once the packet limit is reached.
551: 	out *clabcapture.Output
552: 
553: 	segment  time.Duration
554: 	overlap  time.Duration
555: 	window   time.Duration
556: 	deadline time.Time
557: }

560: // reached and the capture stops.

562: 	return run.out.Emit(id, packet)

564: 
565: func (run *captureRun) reportGap(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) {
566: 	clabcapture.ReportGap(run.req.OnGap, gap)
567: }
568: 
569: // captureSegment is one clabwire capture process of a chain.
570: type captureSegment struct {
571: 	index      int
572: 	localStart time.Time
573: 	duration   time.Duration
574: 	cancel     context.CancelFunc
575: 	// closeStdin closes the stdin of the segment's clabwire process, which ends it; it may be
576: 	// called any number of times.
577: 	closeStdin func()
578: 	// stopTimer closes stdin once the segment is no longer needed after a switch-over.
579: 	stopTimer *time.Timer
580: 	// started and ended are the pod-clock times of the Started and Succeeded audit records.
581: 	started time.Time
582: 	ended   time.Time
583: 	done    bool
584: }
585: 
586: func (s *captureSegment) plannedEnd() time.Time {
587: 	return s.started.Add(s.duration)
588: }
589: 
590: // segmentEvent is something a segment reported: a packet, an audit record, or its end.
591: type segmentEvent struct {
592: 	segment *captureSegment
593: 	packet  *clabcapture.Packet
594: 	audit   *captureAudit
595: 	done    bool
596: 	err     error
597: }
598: 
599: // captureChain runs the chained clabwire captures of one group.
600: //
601: // Chaining and the cut: segment k+1 starts `overlap` before segment k is due to end, so both
602: // capture the same packets for a while. clabwire stamps packets when it reads them, so two
603: // processes give the same packet timestamps a few microseconds apart, and timestamps alone
604: // cannot pair them. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by
605: // content close to the cut:
606: //
607: //  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is
608: //     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.
609: //  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the
610: //     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.
611: //  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped
612: //     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped
613: //     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.
614: //     From then on segment k+1 streams live.
615: //
616: // Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its
617: // planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other
618: // nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.
619: //
620: // W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. Identical frames on
621: // the same interface within W of the cut can be paired with each other, which can drop a true
622: // repeat; nothing else is lost or doubled. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves
623: // a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.
624: type captureChain struct {
625: 	capture *captureRun
626: 	group   *captureGroup
627: 
628: 	events chan segmentEvent
629: 	wg     sync.WaitGroup
630: 
631: 	active *captureSegment
632: 	next   *captureSegment
633: 	// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.
634: 	cut int64
635: 	// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.
636: 	emitted map[uint64]int
637: 	// held are the packets of next until active ends.
638: 	held     []*clabcapture.Packet
639: 	segments int
640: 	retries  int
641: 	// final is set once no further segment is due.
642: 	final bool
643: 	// stopping is set once ctx ended: the segments are asked to end and what they still
644: 	// deliver is written.
645: 	stopping bool
646: }
647: 
648: // run runs the chain until its last segment ended. When ctx ends, it stops the segments and
649: // keeps writing the packets they read until then; a segment that does not end within
650: // captureStdinCloseGrace is cut.
651: func (c *captureChain) run(ctx context.Context) error {
652: 	c.events = make(chan segmentEvent, 256)
653: 	// the segments outlive ctx so they can deliver their last packets; segmentsCtx cuts them
654: 	segmentsCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))
655: 	var abort *time.Timer
656: 	defer func() {
657: 		if abort != nil {
658: 			abort.Stop()
659: 		}
660: 		cancel()
661: 		c.drain()
662: 		c.capture.out.Release(c)
663: 	}()
664: 
665: 	c.active = c.start(segmentsCtx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
666: 	timer := time.NewTimer(c.nextStartIn())
667: 	defer timer.Stop()
668: 
669: 	done := ctx.Done()
670: 	for {
671: 		select {
672: 		case <-done:
673: 			done = nil
674: 			c.stop(timer)
675: 			abort = time.AfterFunc(captureStdinCloseGrace, cancel)
676: 		case <-segmentsCtx.Done():
677: 			return nil
678: 		case <-timer.C:
679: 			if c.next == nil && !c.final {
680: 				c.startNext(segmentsCtx)
681: 			}
682: 		case event := <-c.events:
683: 			stop, err := c.handle(segmentsCtx, event, timer)
684: 			if err != nil || stop {
685: 				return err
686: 			}
687: 		}
688: 	}
689: }
690: 
691: // stop ends the chain early, like a deadline would: no further segment starts and the running
692: // ones are asked to end. The chain then writes what they deliver until they ended.
693: func (c *captureChain) stop(timer *time.Timer) {
694: 	c.stopping = true
695: 	c.final = true
696: 	timer.Stop()
697: 	c.active.closeStdin()
698: 	if c.next != nil {
699: 		c.next.closeStdin()
700: 	}
701: }
702: 
703: // drain waits for the segment goroutines after the chain ended.
704: func (c *captureChain) drain() {
705: 	done := make(chan struct{})
706: 	go func() {
707: 		c.wg.Wait()
708: 		close(done)
709: 	}()
710: 	for {
711: 		select {
712: 		case <-done:
713: 			return
714: 		case <-c.events:
715: 		}
716: 	}
717: }
718: 
719: // segmentDuration is the requested duration of a segment starting now.
720: func (c *captureChain) segmentDuration(now time.Time) time.Duration {
721: 	duration := c.capture.segment
722: 	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() {
723: 		duration = min(duration, c.capture.deadline.Sub(now))
724: 	}
725: 
726: 	return max(duration, minCaptureSegment)
727: }
728: 
729: // nextStartIn is the time until the follow-up of the active segment is due. It marks the chain
730: // final when none is due.
731: func (c *captureChain) nextStartIn() time.Duration {
732: 	if c.stopping {
733: 		c.final = true
734: 		return maxCaptureSegment
735: 	}
736: 	activeEnd := c.active.localStart.Add(c.active.duration)
737: 	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
738: 		!activeEnd.Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
739: 		c.final = true
740: 		return maxCaptureSegment
741: 	}
742: 	c.final = false
743: 
744: 	return max(time.Until(activeEnd.Add(-c.capture.overlap)), 0)
745: }
746: 
747: func (c *captureChain) startNext(ctx context.Context) {
748: 	c.next = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
749: 	c.emitted = map[uint64]int{}
750: 	c.held = nil
751: 	c.cut = 0
752: }
753: 
754: func (c *captureChain) handle(
755: 	ctx context.Context,
756: 	event segmentEvent,
757: 	timer *time.Timer,
758: ) (bool, error) {
759: 	segment := event.segment
760: 
761: 	switch {
762: 	case event.audit != nil:
763: 		return false, c.handleAudit(segment, event.audit)
764: 	case event.packet != nil:
765: 		return c.handlePacket(segment, event.packet)
766: 	case event.done:
767: 		segment.done = true
768: 		if segment.stopTimer != nil {
769: 			segment.stopTimer.Stop()
770: 		}
771: 		if event.err != nil && !c.stopping {
772: 			if segment == c.next && segment.started.IsZero() && c.retries < captureStartRetries {
773: 				// the follow-up did not start; try again while the active one still runs
774: 				c.retries++
775: 				log.Warn("Capture follow-up segment failed to start, retrying",
776: 					"node", c.group.display, "error", event.err)
777: 				c.next = nil
778: 				resetTimer(timer, time.Second)
779: 
780: 				return false, nil
781: 			}
782: 
783: 			return true, fmt.Errorf("capture on c9s node %s/%s/%s failed: %w",
784: 				c.group.location.Namespace, c.capture.req.Name, c.group.display, event.err)
785: 		}
786: 		if segment != c.active {
787: 			return false, nil
788: 		}
789: 
790: 		return c.switchSegments(ctx, timer)
791: 	}
792: 
793: 	return false, nil
794: }
795: 
796: func (c *captureChain) handleAudit(segment *captureSegment, audit *captureAudit) error {
797: 	switch audit.Status {
798: 	case captureAuditStarted:
799: 		segment.started = audit.Time
800: 		log.Debug("Capture segment started", "node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index,
801: 			"interfaces", strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ","), "duration", segment.duration)
802: 		if segment == c.next && !c.active.started.IsZero() {
803: 			c.setCut()
804: 		}
805: 		if segment == c.next {
806: 			c.retries = 0
807: 		}
808: 	case captureAuditSucceeded:
809: 		segment.ended = audit.Time
810: 		log.Debug("Capture segment succeeded", "node", c.group.display,
811: 			"segment", segment.index, "packets", audit.Packets)
812: 	case captureAuditDenied, captureAuditFailed:
813: 		return captureAuditError(c.group.display, audit)
814: 	}
815: 
816: 	return nil
817: }
818: 
819: // captureAuditError turns a Denied or Failed clabwire audit record into an error.
820: func captureAuditError(node string, audit *captureAudit) error {
821: 	verb := "failed"
822: 	if audit.Status == captureAuditDenied {
823: 		verb = "was denied"
824: 	}
825: 	interfaces := make([]string, 0, len(audit.Interfaces))
826: 	for _, intf := range audit.Interfaces {
827: 		interfaces = append(interfaces, intf.Name)
828: 	}
829: 
830: 	return fmt.Errorf("capture of %s on node %s %s by clabwire: %s",
831: 		strings.Join(interfaces, ","), node, verb, audit.Reason)
832: }
833: 
834: // setCut places the cut in the middle of the overlap of the active and the next segment, both
835: // measured on the pod clock.
836: func (c *captureChain) setCut() {
837: 	overlapStart := c.next.started
838: 	overlapEnd := c.active.plannedEnd()
839: 	if overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) < 2*c.capture.window {
840: 		// the overlap is too short to match packets around a cut: the switch is reported as a
841: 		// gap once the active segment ended
842: 		c.cut = 0
843: 		return
844: 	}
845: 	c.cut = overlapStart.Add(overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) / 2).UnixNano()
846: 
847: 	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
848: 	// Packets the next segment holds back are stamped from T-W on: other chains' packets after
849: 	// that wait in the reorder buffer until the switch, so the merged stream stays in order.
850: 	c.capture.out.Hold(c, c.cut-window)
851: 
852: 	// The active segment only matters for packets stamped before T. Once the pod clock passed
853: 	// T+W, it is closed: packets it read until then are still delivered, and the ones it reads
854: 	// later are stamped after T and dropped anyway. The next segment's Started record was
855: 	// written on the pod clock no later than now, so the pod clock passes T+W no later than
856: 	// (T - Started + W) from now.
857: 	active := c.active
858: 	active.stopTimer = time.AfterFunc(
859: 		time.Duration(c.cut-c.next.started.UnixNano()+window), active.closeStdin)
860: }
861: 
862: func (c *captureChain) handlePacket(
863: 	segment *captureSegment,
864: 	packet *clabcapture.Packet,
865: ) (bool, error) {
866: 	switch segment {
867: 	case c.active:
868: 		if c.cut != 0 && packet.Timestamp >= c.cut {
869: 			return false, nil
870: 		}
871: 		if c.next != nil {
872: 			c.emitted[packetKey(packet)]++
873: 		}
874: 
875: 		return c.emit(packet)
876: 	case c.next:
877: 		c.held = append(c.held, packet)
878: 	}
879: 
880: 	return false, nil
881: }
882: 
883: func (c *captureChain) emit(packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {
884: 	if int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(c.group.ids) {
885: 		return true, fmt.Errorf("clabwire wrote a packet for interface %d of %d",
886: 			packet.InterfaceID, len(c.group.ids))
887: 	}
888: 	more, err := c.capture.emit(c.group.ids[packet.InterfaceID], packet)
889: 
890: 	return !more, err
891: }
892: 
893: // switchSegments makes the next segment the active one after the active one ended, writing the
894: // held packets of the next one that the active one did not write.
895: func (c *captureChain) switchSegments(ctx context.Context, timer *time.Timer) (bool, error) {
896: 	// the held packets are in the reorder buffer once this returns
897: 	defer c.capture.out.Release(c)
898: 
899: 	ended := c.active
900: 	if c.stopping && c.next != nil && c.next.started.IsZero() {
901: 		// the chain is stopping: a follow-up that has not started takes nothing over
902: 		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
903: 	}
904: 	if c.final && c.next == nil {
905: 		return true, nil
906: 	}
907: 
908: 	if c.next == nil || c.next.started.IsZero() || c.cut == 0 {
909: 		from := ended.ended
910: 		if from.IsZero() {
911: 			from = ended.plannedEnd()
912: 		}
913: 		gap := clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
914: 			Node: c.group.display, Interfaces: c.group.interfaces, From: from,
915: 			Reason: "the follow-up capture did not overlap the previous one",
916: 		}
917: 		if c.next != nil && !c.next.started.IsZero() {
918: 			gap.To = c.next.started
919: 		}
920: 		c.capture.reportGap(gap)
921: 	}
922: 
923: 	if c.next != nil && c.next.done && !c.stopping {
924: 		// the follow-up already ended (it started too late to take over): keep what it
925: 		// captured and continue with a fresh segment
926: 		for _, packet := range c.held {
927: 			if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
928: 				return true, err
929: 			}
930: 		}
931: 		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
932: 	}
933: 
934: 	if c.next == nil {
935: 		if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
936: 			!time.Now().Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
937: 			return true, nil
938: 		}
939: 		c.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
940: 		resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
941: 
942: 		return false, nil
943: 	}
944: 
945: 	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
946: 	for _, packet := range c.held {
947: 		if c.cut != 0 {
948: 			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut-window {
949: 				continue
950: 			}
951: 			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut+window {
952: 				key := packetKey(packet)
953: 				if c.emitted[key] > 0 {
954: 					c.emitted[key]--
955: 					continue
956: 				}
957: 			}
958: 		}
959: 		if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
960: 			return true, err
961: 		}
962: 	}
963: 
964: 	c.active, c.next = c.next, nil
965: 	c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, 0
966: 	if c.active.done {
967: 		// the chain is stopping and the follow-up ended before the active one
968: 		return true, nil
969: 	}
970: 	resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
971: 
972: 	return false, nil
973: }
974: 
975: func resetTimer(timer *time.Timer, d time.Duration) {
976: 	if !timer.Stop() {
977: 		select {
978: 		case <-timer.C:
979: 		default:
980: 		}
981: 	}
982: 	timer.Reset(d)
983: }
984: 
985: // packetKey identifies a packet by its interface and content.
986: func packetKey(packet *clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {
987: 	hash := fnv.New64a()
988: 	var id [4]byte
989: 	id[0] = byte(packet.InterfaceID)
990: 	id[1] = byte(packet.InterfaceID >> 8)
991: 	_, _ = hash.Write(id[:])
992: 	_, _ = hash.Write(packet.Data)
993: 
994: 	return hash.Sum64()
995: }
996: 
997: // start runs one clabwire capture and reports its packets, audit records and end as events.
998: func (c *captureChain) start(ctx context.Context, duration time.Duration) *captureSegment {
999: 	segmentCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
1000: 	stdinReader, stdinWriter := io.Pipe()
1001: 	segment := &captureSegment{
1002: 		index: c.segments, localStart: time.Now(), duration: duration, cancel: cancel,
1003: 		closeStdin: func() { _ = stdinWriter.Close() },
1004: 	}
1005: 	c.segments++
1006: 
1007: 	command := []string{
1008: 		clabwireManager, "node-runtime", "packet-capture",
1009: 		"--nodeName", c.group.location.NodeName,
1010: 		"--format", "pcapng",
1011: 		"--snapLength", strconv.Itoa(c.capture.req.SnapLength),
1012: 		"--duration", duration.String(),
1013: 		clabwireStopOnStdinClose,
1014: 	}
1015: 	for _, name := range c.group.interfaces {
1016: 		command = append(command, "--interface", name)
1017: 	}
1018: 	if c.capture.req.PacketLimit > 0 {
1019: 		remaining := int64(c.capture.req.PacketLimit) - c.capture.out.Written()
1020: 		command = append(command, "--packetLimit",
1021: 			strconv.FormatInt(min(max(remaining, 1), maxClabwirePackets), 10))
1022: 	}
1023: 
1024: 	send := func(event segmentEvent) {
1025: 		event.segment = segment
1026: 		select {
1027: 		case c.events <- event:
1028: 		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
1029: 		}
1030: 	}
1031: 
1032: 	stdoutReader, stdoutWriter := io.Pipe()
1033: 	stderr := &auditLineWriter{send: func(audit *captureAudit) { send(segmentEvent{audit: audit}) }}
1034: 
1035: 	// The exec outlives the segment's context by up to captureStdinCloseGrace: when the segment
1036: 	// ends for any reason (the capture is cancelled or failed, the output failed, or a newer
1037: 	// segment took over), its stdin is closed first so clabwire ends on its own, and the stream
1038: 	// is cut only if it does not.
1039: 	execCtx, cancelExec := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(segmentCtx))
1040: 	execDone := make(chan struct{})
1041: 
1042: 	c.wg.Add(3)
1043: 	readDone := make(chan error, 1)
1044: 	go func() {
1045: 		defer c.wg.Done()
1046: 		readDone <- c.readSegment(stdoutReader, func(packet *clabcapture.Packet) {
1047: 			send(segmentEvent{packet: packet})
1048: 		})
1049: 		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, stdoutReader)
1050: 	}()
1051: 	go func() {
1052: 		defer c.wg.Done()
1053: 		select {
1054: 		case <-execDone:
1055: 			return
1056: 		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
1057: 		}
1058: 		segment.closeStdin()
1059: 		grace := time.NewTimer(captureStdinCloseGrace)
1060: 		defer grace.Stop()
1061: 		select {
1062: 		case <-execDone:
1063: 		case <-grace.C:
1064: 			log.Debug("Capture segment did not end after its stdin closed, cutting the stream",
1065: 				"node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index)
1066: 			cancelExec()
1067: 		}
1068: 	}()
1069: 	go func() {
1070: 		defer c.wg.Done()
1071: 		defer cancel()
1072: 		defer cancelExec()
1073: 
1074: 		err := c.capture.r.execInPodContainer()(execCtx, c.group.location.Namespace,
1075: 			c.group.location.Pod, clabwireContainer, command, stdinReader, stdoutWriter, stderr)
1076: 		close(execDone)
1077: 		// the process ended: release the stdin copy of the exec stream
1078: 		segment.closeStdin()
1079: 		_ = stdoutWriter.Close()
1080: 		readErr := <-readDone
1081: 		stderr.flush()
1082: 		if err == nil && readErr != nil {
1083: 			err = readErr
1084: 		}
1085: 		if err != nil && stderr.text() != "" {
1086: 			if unsupported := unsupportedClabwire(
1087: 				c.group.location,
1088: 				stderr.text(),
1089: 			); unsupported != nil {
1090: 				err = unsupported
1091: 			} else {
1092: 				err = fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, stderr.text())
1093: 			}
1094: 		}
1095: 		send(segmentEvent{done: true, err: err})
1096: 	}()
1097: 
1098: 	return segment
1099: }
1100: 
1101: // unsupportedClabwire recognizes a clabwire that rejects --stop-on-stdin-close, which every
1102: // capture passes: its release predates the capture contract the runtime needs.
1103: func unsupportedClabwire(location clablabruntime.NodeLocation, stderr string) error {
1104: 	if !strings.Contains(stderr, "flag provided but not defined") ||
1105: 		!strings.Contains(stderr, strings.TrimPrefix(clabwireStopOnStdinClose, "-")) {
1106: 		return nil
1107: 	}
1108: 
1109: 	return &unsupportedClabernetesError{reason: fmt.Sprintf(
1110: 		"clabwire in pod %s/%s does not accept packet-capture %s",
1111: 		location.Namespace, location.Pod, clabwireStopOnStdinClose)}
1112: }
1113: 
1114: // readSegment checks that a segment's interfaces are the requested ones and passes its packets
1115: // on with the segment's interface index.
1116: func (c *captureChain) readSegment(stdout io.Reader, packet func(*clabcapture.Packet)) error {
1117: 	reader := clabcapture.NewReader(stdout)
1118: 	interfaces := 0
1119: 	for {
1120: 		event, err := reader.Next()
1121: 		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
1122: 			return nil
1123: 		}
1124: 		if errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) {
1125: 			// the process was stopped inside a block
1126: 			return nil
1127: 		}
1128: 		if err != nil {
1129: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read the clabwire capture: %w", err)
1130: 		}
1131: 		if event.Interface != nil {

1157: 	w.mu.Lock()
1158: 	w.partial = append(w.partial, data...)
1159: 	var lines [][]byte
1160: 	for {
1161: 		idx := bytes.IndexByte(w.partial, '\n')

1165: 		lines = append(lines, append([]byte(nil), w.partial[:idx]...))
1166: 		w.partial = w.partial[idx+1:]

1168: 	w.mu.Unlock()
1169: 
1170: 	for _, line := range lines {
1171: 		w.line(line)
1172: 	}

1174: 	return len(data), nil
1175: }

1177: func (w *auditLineWriter) flush() {
1178: 	w.mu.Lock()

1181: 	w.mu.Unlock()

1203: 	w.mu.Lock()
1204: 	defer w.mu.Unlock()
1205: 	if len(w.other) < 20 {
1206: 		w.other = append(w.other, string(line))
1207: 	}
1208: }

1211: 	w.mu.Lock()

writeErr != nil {\n536: \t\treturn writeErr\n537: \t}\n538: \tif err != nil && !(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && captureCtx.Err() != nil) {\n539: \t\treturn err\n540: \t}\n541: \n542: \treturn nil\n543: }\n544: \n545: // captureRun is the state a capture's chains share.\n546: type captureRun struct {\n547: \tr   *Runtime\n548: \treq clablabruntime.CaptureRequest\n549: \t// out is the merged stream; it writes the packets of every chain in timestamp order and\n550: \t// stops every chain once the packet limit is reached.\n551: \tout *clabcapture.Output\n552: \n553: \tsegment  time.Duration\n554: \toverlap  time.Duration\n555: \twindow   time.Duration\n556: \tdeadline time.Time\n557: }\n558: \n559: // emit writes a packet under its merged interface ID. It reports false once the packet limit is\n560: // reached and the capture stops.\n561: func (run *captureRun) emit(id uint32, packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {\n562: \treturn run.out.Emit(id, packet)\n563: }\n564: \n565: func (run *captureRun) reportGap(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) {\n566: \tclabcapture.ReportGap(run.req.OnGap, gap)\n567: }\n568: \n569: // captureSegment is one clabwire capture process of a chain.\n570: type captureSegment struct {\n571: \tindex      int\n572: \tlocalStart time.Time\n573: \tduration   time.Duration\n574: \tcancel     context.CancelFunc\n575: \t// closeStdin closes the stdin of the segment's clabwire process, which ends it; it may be\n576: \t// called any number of times.\n577: \tcloseStdin func()\n578: \t// stopTimer closes stdin once the segment is no longer needed after a switch-over.\n579: \tstopTimer *time.Timer\n580: \t// started and ended are the pod-clock times of the Started and Succeeded audit records.\n581: \tstarted time.Time\n582: \tended   time.Time\n583: \tdone    bool\n584: }\n585: \n586: func (s *captureSegment) plannedEnd() time.Time {\n587: \treturn s.started.Add(s.duration)\n588: }\n589: \n590: // segmentEvent is something a segment reported: a packet, an audit record, or its end.\n591: type segmentEvent struct {\n592: \tsegment *captureSegment\n593: \tpacket  *clabcapture.Packet\n594: \taudit   *captureAudit\n595: \tdone    bool\n596: \terr     error\n597: }\n598: \n599: // captureChain runs the chained clabwire captures of one group.\n600: //\n601: // Chaining and the cut: segment k+1 starts `overlap` before segment k is due to end, so both\n602: // capture the same packets for a while. clabwire stamps packets when it reads them, so two\n603: // processes give the same packet timestamps a few microseconds apart, and timestamps alone\n604: // cannot pair them. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by\n605: // content close to the cut:\n606: //\n607: //  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is\n608: //     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.\n609: //  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the\n610: //     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.\n611: //  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped\n612: //     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped\n613: //     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.\n614: //     From then on segment k+1 streams live.\n615: //\n616: // Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its\n617: // planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other\n618: // nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.\n619: //\n620: // W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. Identical frames on\n621: // the same interface within W of the cut can be paired with each other, which can drop a true\n622: // repeat; nothing else is lost or doubled. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves\n623: // a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.\n624: type captureChain struct {\n625: \tcapture *captureRun\n626: \tgroup   *captureGroup\n627: \n628: \tevents chan segmentEvent\n629: \twg     sync.WaitGroup\n630: \n631: \tactive *captureSegment\n632: \tnext   *captureSegment\n633: \t// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.\n634: \tcut int64\n635: \t// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.\n636: \temitted map[uint64]int\n637: \t// held are the packets of next until active ends.\n638: \theld     []*clabcapture.Packet\n639: \tsegments int\n640: \tretries  int\n641: \t// final is set once no further segment is due.\n642: \tfinal bool\n643: \t// stopping is set once ctx ended: the segments are asked to end and what they still\n644: \t// deliver is written.\n645: \tstopping bool\n646: }\n647: \n648: // run runs the chain until its last segment ended. A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error.\nfunc (r *Runtime) Capture(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\treq clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,\n\tw io.Writer,\n) error {\n\tif err := clabcapture.ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tr, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tresolved, err := r.resolveCaptureTargets(ctx, req)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tcaptureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)\n\tdefer stop()\n\n\tout, err := clabcapture.NewOutput(w, resolved.names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit,\n\t\tr.captureReorderWindowLength(), stop)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\trun := &captureRun{\n\t\tr:       r,\n\t\treq:     req,\n\t\tout:     out,\n\t\tsegment: r.captureSegmentLength(),\n\t}\n\tif req.Duration > 0 {\n\t\trun.deadline = time.Now().Add(req.Duration)\n\t}\n\trun.overlap = min(maxCaptureOverlap, run.segment/3)\n\trun.window = min(maxCaptureCutWindow, run.overlap/4)\n\n\tif req.Duration > 0 {\n\t\t// a clabwire process that does not end on its own does not hold the capture open\n\t\tvar cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc\n\t\tcaptureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx,\n\t\t\treq.Duration+run.overlap+captureEndGrace)\n\t\tdefer cancelTimeout()\n\t}\n\n\tgroup, groupCtx := errgroup.WithContext(captureCtx)\n\tfor _, captureGroup := range resolved.groups {\n\t\tchain := &captureChain{capture: run, group: captureGroup}\n\t\tgroup.Go(func() error {\n\t\t\treturn chain.run(groupCtx)\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\n\terr = group.Wait()\n\tif writeErr := out.Close(); writeErr != nil {\n\t\treturn writeErr\n\t}\n\tif err != nil && !(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && captureCtx.Err() != nil) {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// captureRun is the state a capture's chains share.\ntype captureRun struct {\n\tr   *Runtime\n\treq clablabruntime.CaptureRequest\n\t// out is the merged stream; it writes the packets of every chain in timestamp order and\n\t// stops every chain once the packet limit is reached.\n\tout *clabcapture.Output\n\n\tsegment  time.Duration\n\toverlap  time.Duration\n\twindow   time.Duration\n\tdeadline time.Time\n}\n\n// emit writes a packet under its merged interface ID. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves\n// a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.\ntype captureChain struct {\n\tcapture *captureRun\n\tgroup   *captureGroup\n\n\tevents chan segmentEvent\n\twg     sync.WaitGroup\n\n\tactive *captureSegment\n\tnext   *captureSegment\n\t// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.\n\tcut int64\n\t// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.\n\temitted map[uint64]int\n\t// held are the packets of next until active ends.\n\theld     []*clabcapture.Packet\n\tsegments int\n\tretries  int\n\t// final is set once no further segment is due.\n\tfinal bool\n\t// stopping is set once ctx ended: the segments are asked to end and what they still\n\t// deliver is written.\n\tstopping bool\n}\n\n// run runs the chain until its last segment ended. 149: func (r *Runtime) pollInterfaces(
150: 	ctx context.Context,
151: 	scope eventScope,
152: 	opts interfacePollOptions,
153: 	eventSink chan<- clablabruntime.Event,
154: ) {
155: 	if opts.interval <= 0 {
156: 		opts.interval = time.Second
157: 	}
158: 
159: 	poller := newInterfacePoller(r, scope, opts, eventSink)
160: 	poller.round(ctx)
161: 
162: 	ticker := time.NewTicker(opts.interval)
163: 	defer ticker.Stop()
164: 
165: 	for {
166: 		select {
167: 		case <-ctx.Done():
168: 			return
169: 		case <-ticker.C:
170: 			poller.round(ctx)
171: 		}
172: 	}
173: }

241: 		p.processSample(ctx, sample)
242: 	}

244: 	p.retireStoppedNodes(ctx, running)
245: 	p.forgetListings(pods)

251: 	for key, tracked := range p.nodes {

349: // sampledInterfaceNames lists the interface names a sample saw, sorted and comma-joined.
350: func sampledInterfaceNames(sample interfaceSample) string {
351: 	names := make([]string, 0, len(sample.stats)+len(sample.ifaces))
352: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
353: 	for _, iface := range sample.ifaces {
354: 		if !seen[iface.Name] {
355: 			seen[iface.Name] = true
356: 			names = append(names, iface.Name)
357: 		}
358: 	}
359: 	for _, stat := range sample.stats {
360: 		if !seen[stat.Name] {
361: 			seen[stat.Name] = true
362: 			names = append(names, stat.Name)
363: 		}
364: 	}
365: 	sort.Strings(names)
366: 
367: 	return strings.Join(names, ",")
368: }

370: // nodeLinks returns the lab link interfaces of a node from its pod's clabwire listing. A pod is
371: // listed once, and again when its interfaces change (a pod gets its link interfaces as clabwire
372: // wires them).
373: func (p *interfacePoller) nodeLinks(
374: 	ctx context.Context,
375: 	target interfaceSampleTarget,
376: 	names string,
377: ) ([]clabwireInterface, error) {
378: 	key := target.pod.Namespace + "/" + target.pod.Name
379: 
380: 	p.listingsMu.Lock()
381: 	listing := p.listings[key]
382: 	p.listingsMu.Unlock()
383: 
384: 	if listing == nil || listing.names != names {
385: 		entries, err := p.r.listPodInterfaces(ctx, target.pod.Namespace, target.pod.Name)
386: 		if err != nil {
387: 			return nil, err
388: 		}
389: 
390: 		listing = &podInterfaceListing{

392: 			byNode: map[string][]clabwireInterface{},
393: 		}
394: 		for _, entry := range entries {
395: 			listing.byNode[entry.Node] = append(listing.byNode[entry.Node], entry)
396: 		}
397: 
398: 		p.listingsMu.Lock()
399: 		p.listings[key] = listing
400: 		p.listingsMu.Unlock()
401: 	}
402: 
403: 	return listing.byNode[target.node.Name], nil
404: }
