406: // commandNotExecutable reports an exec that failed because the command does not exist in the

409: 	if rc == exitCommandNotExecutable || rc == exitCommandNotFound {
410: 		return true
411: 	}

427: 	return reported
428: }

430: // interfaceEventData describes an interface the way the local runtimes' netlink events do: the
431: // alias is the topology's name for the interface (an alias clabernetes set for its own use is
432: // not reported), the operational state uses netlink's names, lab link and management
433: // interfaces are veth pairs, loopback a device, and loopback has no hardware address.
434: func interfaceEventData(iface c9sIfaceState, alias string) clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData {
435: 	if alias == "" && !strings.HasPrefix(iface.Alias, clabernetesAliasPrefix) {
436: 		alias = iface.Alias
437: 	}
438: 
439: 	mac := iface.MAC
440: 	if mac == zeroMAC {
441: 		mac = ""
442: 	}
443: 
444: 	linkType := interfaceTypeVeth
445: 	if iface.Name == loopbackInterface {
446: 		linkType = interfaceTypeDevice
447: 	}
448: 
449: 	return clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData{
450: 		Name:      iface.Name,
451: 		Alias:     alias,
452: 		Index:     iface.Index,
453: 		MTU:       iface.MTU,
454: 		MAC:       mac,
455: 		OperState: netlinkOperState(iface.OperState),
456: 		Type:      linkType,
457: 	}
458: }
459: 
460: // netlinkOperState names an operational state from sysfs (RFC 2863, as in
461: // /sys/class/net/<if>/operstate) the way netlink, and so the local runtimes' events, name it.
462: func netlinkOperState(operState string) string {
463: 	switch operState {
464: 	case "notpresent":
465: 		return "not-present"
466: 	case "lowerlayerdown":
467: 		return "lower-layer-down"
468: 	case "":
469: 		return "unknown"
470: 	default:
471: 		return operState
472: 	}
473: }

475: func (p *interfacePoller) processSample(ctx context.Context, sample interfaceSample) {
476: 	state := sample.target.state
477: 	node := sample.target.node
478: 	key := c9sNodeKey(state.Namespace, state.Name, node.Name)
479: 
480: 	tracked, known := p.nodes[key]
481: 	if !known {
482: 		tracked = &trackedNode{ifaces: map[string]clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData{}}
483: 		p.nodes[key] = tracked
484: 	}
485: 	tracked.lab = state
486: 	tracked.node = node
487: 
488: 	reported := reportedInterfaces(sample.links)
489: 
490: 	if sample.hasStates {
491: 		p.processStates(ctx, tracked, reported, sample)
492: 	}
493: 
494: 	if !p.opts.includeStats {
495: 		return
496: 	}
497: 	for _, stat := range sample.stats {
498: 		alias, ok := reported[stat.Name]
499: 		if !ok {
500: 			continue
501: 		}
502: 
503: 		statsKey := c9sIfaceStatsKey(state.Namespace, state.Name, node.Name, stat.Name)
504: 		current := c9sIfaceStatsSample{Stats: stat, Timestamp: sample.timestamp}
505: 		if previous, ok := p.statsSamples[statsKey]; ok {
506: 			data, ok := tracked.ifaces[stat.Name]
507: 			if !ok {
508: 				data = interfaceEventData(c9sIfaceState{Name: stat.Name}, alias)
509: 				data.OperState = ""
510: 			}
511: 			data.Stats = c9sIfaceStatsData(previous, current)
512: 			p.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionStats, data, current.Timestamp)
513: 		}
514: 
515: 		p.statsSamples[statsKey] = current
516: 	}
517: }
518: 
519: // processStates reports the interfaces that appeared (snapshot in the first round with
520: // --initial-state, create later), changed (update) or disappeared (delete) since the last
521: // sample, like the netlink events of the local runtimes.
522: func (p *interfacePoller) processStates(
523: 	ctx context.Context,
524: 	tracked *trackedNode,
525: 	reported map[string]string,
526: 	sample interfaceSample,
527: ) {
528: 	present := map[string]bool{}
529: 	for _, iface := range sample.ifaces {
530: 		alias, ok := reported[iface.Name]
531: 		if !ok {
532: 			continue
533: 		}
534: 
535: 		data := interfaceEventData(iface, alias)
536: 		present[iface.Name] = true
537: 		previous, seen := tracked.ifaces[iface.Name]
538: 		tracked.ifaces[iface.Name] = data
539: 
540: 		switch {
541: 		case seen && previous == data:
542: 		case !seen && p.firstRound:
543: 			// Interfaces that exist when the stream starts are only reported with
544: 			// --initial-state; later changes are always reported.
545: 			if p.opts.includeInitialState {
546: 				p.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionSnapshot, data, sample.timestamp)
547: 			}
548: 		case !seen:
549: 			p.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionCreate, data, sample.timestamp)
550: 		default:
551: 			p.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionUpdate, data, sample.timestamp)
552: 		}
553: 	}
554: 
555: 	for _, name := range sortedInterfaceNames(tracked.ifaces) {
556: 		if present[name] {
557: 			continue
558: 		}
559: 
560: 		p.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionDelete, tracked.ifaces[name], sample.timestamp)
561: 		p.forgetStats(tracked, name)
562: 		delete(tracked.ifaces, name)
563: 	}
564: }
565: 
566: func sortedInterfaceNames(ifaces map[string]clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData) []string {
567: 	names := make([]string, 0, len(ifaces))
568: 	for name := range ifaces {
569: 		names = append(names, name)
570: 	}
571: 	sort.Strings(names)
572: 
573: 	return names
574: }
575: 
576: func (p *interfacePoller) forgetStats(tracked *trackedNode, ifName string) {
577: 	delete(p.statsSamples,
578: 		c9sIfaceStatsKey(tracked.lab.Namespace, tracked.lab.Name, tracked.node.Name, ifName))
579: }

581: func (p *interfacePoller) emit(
582: 	ctx context.Context,
583: 	tracked *trackedNode,
584: 	action string,
585: 	data clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData,
586: 	timestamp time.Time,
587: ) {
588: 	p.r.sendEvent(ctx, p.sink, c9sInterfaceEvent(tracked, action, data, timestamp))
589: }

591: // c9sInterfaceEvent is an interface event of a node. The actor is the node, as for its container
592: // events. The interface itself is in Interface; the events command reports it with the
593: // attributes of the local runtimes' interface events.
594: func c9sInterfaceEvent(
595: 	tracked *trackedNode,
596: 	action string,
597: 	data clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData,
598: 	timestamp time.Time,
599: ) clablabruntime.Event {
600: 	key := c9sNodeKey(tracked.lab.Namespace, tracked.lab.Name, tracked.node.Name)
601: 
602: 	attributes := map[string]string{
603: 		"namespace": tracked.lab.Namespace,
604: 		"lab":       tracked.lab.Name,
605: 		"node":      tracked.node.Name,
606: 		"origin":    clabernetesAppValue,
607: 	}
608: 	if tracked.node.Pod != "" {
609: 		attributes["pod"] = tracked.node.Pod
610: 	}
611: 
612: 	node := tracked.node
613: 
614: 	return clablabruntime.Event{
615: 		Timestamp:   timestamp,
616: 		Type:        clablabruntime.EventTypeInterface,
617: 		Action:      action,
618: 		ActorID:     key,
619: 		ActorName:   fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", tracked.lab.Name, tracked.node.Name),
620: 		ActorFullID: key,
621: 		Attributes:  attributes,
622: 		Lab:         tracked.lab,
623: 		Node:        &node,
624: 		Interface:   &data,
625: 	}
626: }

628: // c9sIfaceStatsData computes the counters and rates of a stats event from two samples.
629: func c9sIfaceStatsData(previous, current c9sIfaceStatsSample) *clablabruntime.InterfaceStats {
630: 	interval := current.Timestamp.Sub(previous.Timestamp)
631: 	if interval <= 0 {
632: 		interval = time.Second
633: 	}
634: 
635: 	seconds := interval.Seconds()
636: 	stat := current.Stats
637: 
638: 	return &clablabruntime.InterfaceStats{
639: 		RxBytes:   stat.RxBytes,
640: 		TxBytes:   stat.TxBytes,
641: 		RxPackets: stat.RxPackets,
642: 		TxPackets: stat.TxPackets,
643: 		RxBps:     float64(counterDelta(stat.RxBytes, previous.Stats.RxBytes)*8) / seconds,
644: 		TxBps:     float64(counterDelta(stat.TxBytes, previous.Stats.TxBytes)*8) / seconds,
645: 		RxPps:     float64(counterDelta(stat.RxPackets, previous.Stats.RxPackets)) / seconds,
646: 		TxPps:     float64(counterDelta(stat.TxPackets, previous.Stats.TxPackets)) / seconds,
647: 		Interval:  interval,
648: 	}
649: }

651: // parseInterfaceSample splits the output of interfaceSampleScript into the /proc/net/dev
652: // counters and the sysfs interface states. hasStates is false for output without the sysfs
653: // section, such as a plain cat of /proc/net/dev.
654: func parseInterfaceSample(data []byte) ([]c9sIfaceStats, []c9sIfaceState, bool, error) {
655: 	text := string(data)
656: 
657: 	procPart, sysfsPart, hasStates := strings.Cut(text, interfaceSysfsMarker+"\n")
658: 	if !hasStates {
659: 		procPart, _, hasStates = strings.Cut(text, interfaceSysfsMarker)
660: 	}
661: 
662: 	stats, err := parseProcNetDev([]byte(procPart))
663: 	if err != nil {
664: 		return nil, nil, false, err
665: 	}
666: 	if !hasStates {
667: 		return stats, nil, false, nil
668: 	}
669: 
670: 	return stats, parseSysfsInterfaces(sysfsPart), true, nil
671: }
672: 
673: func parseSysfsInterfaces(data string) []c9sIfaceState {
674: 	lines := strings.Split(data, "\n")
675: 	states := make([]c9sIfaceState, 0, len(lines))
676: 
677: 	for _, line := range lines {
678: 		fields := strings.SplitN(line, "\t", 7) //nolint:mnd
679: 		if len(fields) < 5 || strings.TrimSpace(fields[0]) == "" {
680: 			continue
681: 		}
682: 
683: 		state := c9sIfaceState{
684: 			Name:      strings.TrimSpace(fields[0]),
685: 			MAC:       strings.TrimSpace(fields[3]),
686: 			OperState: strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(fields[4])),
687: 		}
688: 		state.Index, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(fields[1]))
689: 		state.MTU, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(fields[2]))
690: 		if len(fields) > 5 {
691: 			state.Flags, _ = strconv.ParseUint(
692: 				strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(fields[5]), "0x"), 16, 64)
693: 		}
694: 		if len(fields) > 6 {
695: 			state.Alias = strings.TrimSpace(fields[6])
696: 		}
697: 		if state.OperState == "" {
698: 			state.OperState = "unknown"
699: 		}
700: 
701: 		states = append(states, state)
702: 	}
703: 
704: 	return states
705: }
706: 
707: func parseProcNetDev(data []byte) ([]c9sIfaceStats, error) {
708: 	lines := strings.Split(string(data), "\n")
709: 	stats := make([]c9sIfaceStats, 0, len(lines))
710: 
711: 	for _, line := range lines {
712: 		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
713: 		if line == "" || !strings.Contains(line, ":") {
714: 			continue
715: 		}
716: 
717: 		parts := strings.SplitN(line, ":", 2)
718: 		if len(parts) != 2 {
719: 			continue
720: 		}
721: 
722: 		ifName := strings.TrimSpace(parts[0])
723: 		fields := strings.Fields(parts[1])
724: 		if len(fields) < 16 {
725: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected /proc/net/dev line for %q: %q", ifName, line)
726: 		}
727: 
728: 		rxBytes, err := strconv.ParseUint(fields[0], 10, 64)
729: 		if err != nil {
730: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse rx bytes for %q: %w", ifName, err)
731: 		}
732: 		rxPackets, err := strconv.ParseUint(fields[1], 10, 64)
733: 		if err != nil {
734: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse rx packets for %q: %w", ifName, err)
735: 		}
736: 		txBytes, err := strconv.ParseUint(fields[8], 10, 64)
737: 		if err != nil {
738: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse tx bytes for %q: %w", ifName, err)
739: 		}
740: 		txPackets, err := strconv.ParseUint(fields[9], 10, 64)
741: 		if err != nil {
742: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse tx packets for %q: %w", ifName, err)
743: 		}
744: 
745: 		stats = append(stats, c9sIfaceStats{
746: 			Name:      ifName,
747: 			RxBytes:   rxBytes,
748: 			RxPackets: rxPackets,
749: 			TxBytes:   txBytes,
750: 			TxPackets: txPackets,
751: 		})
752: 	}
753: 
754: 	return stats, nil
755: }
756: 
757: // c9sNodeKey is the actor ID of a node: <namespace>/<lab>/<node>, the same value inspect
758: // reports as container_id.
759: func c9sNodeKey(namespace, lab, node string) string {
760: 	return namespace + "/" + lab + "/" + node
761: }
762: 
763: func c9sIfaceStatsKey(namespace, lab, node, ifName string) string {
764: 	return c9sNodeKey(namespace, lab, node) + "/" + ifName
765: }
766: 
767: func counterDelta(current, previous uint64) uint64 {
768: 	if current < previous {
769: 		return 0
770: 	}
771: 
772: 	return current - previous
773: }

        "text": "package clabernetes\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"sort\"\n\t\"strconv\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"sync\"\n\t\"time\"\n\n\t\"github.com/charmbracelet/log\"\n\tclablabruntime \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime\"\n\tcorev1 \"k8s.io/api/core/v1\"\n\tmetav1 \"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1\"\n)\n\nconst (\n\t// interfaceSysfsMarker separates the /proc/net/dev counters from the sysfs interface\n\t// attributes in the output of interfaceSampleScript.\n\tinterfaceSysfsMarker = \"@@clab-sysfs\"\n\t// interfaceSampleScript reads the interface counters and, per interface, the sysfs\n\t// attributes the interface state events carry, in one exec:\n\t// name, ifindex, mtu, address, operstate, flags and ifalias, tab separated.\n\tinterfaceSampleScript = `cat /proc/net/dev; echo ` + interfaceSysfsMarker + `; ` +\n\t\t`for d in /sys/class/net/*; do [ -e \"$d/operstate\" ] || continue; ` +\n\t\t`printf '%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\n' \"${d##*/}\" \"$(cat \"$d/ifindex\")\" ` +\n\t\t`\"$(cat \"$d/mtu\")\" \"$(cat \"$d/address\")\" \"$(cat \"$d/operstate\")\" ` +\n\t\t`\"$(cat \"$d/flags\")\" \"$(cat \"$d/ifalias\")\"; done 2>/dev/null`\n\n\t// interfaceSampleWorkers bounds the concurrent execs of one sampling round.\n\tinterfaceSampleWorkers = 16\n\n\t// managementInterface is a node's management interface in its pod, the interface the\n\t// clabernetes planner gives the management address by default. It has the name the\n\t// management interface has in a container of the local runtimes.\n\tmanagementInterface = \"eth0\"\n\t// loopbackInterface is reported like the local runtimes report it.\n\tloopbackInterface = \"lo\"\n\t// clabernetesAliasPrefix starts the interface aliases clabernetes marks its own interfaces\n\t// and the lab links it wires with. They are not the topology's names, so they are not\n\t// reported.\n\tclabernetesAliasPrefix = \"c9s:\"\n\t// zeroMAC is the hardware address sysfs reports for interfaces without one (loopback).\n\tzeroMAC = \"00:00:00:00:00:00\"\n\n\t// Interface event actions and link types, as the local runtimes report them.\n\tinterfaceActionSnapshot = \"snapshot\"\n\tinterfaceActionCreate   = \"create\"\n\tinterfaceActionUpdate   = \"update\"\n\tinterfaceActionDelete   = \"delete\"\n\tinterfaceActionStats    = \"stats\"\n\tinterfaceTypeVeth       = \"veth\"\n\tinterfaceTypeDevice     = \"device\"\n\n\t// shell exit codes of a command that cannot be found or executed.\n\texitCommandNotExecutable = 126\n\texitCommandNotFound      = 127\n)\n\ntype interfacePollOptions struct {\n\tinterval            time.Duration\n\tincludeStats        bool\n\tincludeInitialState bool\n}\n\ntype c9sIfaceStats struct {\n\tName      string\n\tRxBytes   uint64\n\tRxPackets uint64\n\tTxBytes   uint64\n\tTxPackets uint64\n}\n\ntype c9sIfaceStatsSample struct {\n\tStats     c9sIfaceStats\n\tTimestamp time.Time\n}\n\n// c9sIfaceState is the sysfs view of one interface in a device container.\ntype c9sIfaceState struct {\n\tName      string\n\tIndex     int\n\tMTU       int\n\tMAC       string\n\tOperState string\n\tFlags     uint64\n\tAlias     string\n}\n\n// trackedNode remembers the interfaces last reported for a node, so their changes and their\n// removal can be reported, also when the node stops running.\ntype trackedNode struct {\n\tlab    *clablabruntime.LabState\n\tnode   clablabruntime.NodeState\n\tifaces map[string]clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData\n}\n\ntype interfaceSampleTarget struct {\n\tstate *clablabruntime.LabState\n\tnode  clablabruntime.NodeState\n\tpod   *corev1.Pod\n}\n\ntype interfaceSample struct {\n\ttarget    interfaceSampleTarget\n\tstats     []c9sIfaceStats\n\tifaces    []c9sIfaceState\n\thasStates bool\n\t// links are the node's lab link interfaces as clabwire lists them.\n\tlinks     []clabwireInterface\n\ttimestamp time.Time\n\terr       error\n}\n\n// podInterfaceListing is the clabwire interface listing of a pod, per node. It is listed again\n// when the pod's interfaces change.\ntype podInterfaceListing struct {\n\tnames  string\n\tbyNode map[string][]clabwireInterface\n}\n\n// interfacePoller samples the interfaces of every running node in an event scope and turns the\n// samples into interface events. It reports the interfaces a container of the local runtimes\n// has for the same node: the node's lab link interfaces, with the names and aliases clabwire\n// lists for them, the management interface and loopback. The pod's own interfaces (the pod\n// network, clabernetes' interposition and link transport interfaces) are not reported.\ntype interfacePoller struct {\n\tr     *Runtime\n\tscope eventScope\n\topts  interfacePollOptions\n\tsink  chan<- clablabruntime.Event\n\n\tstatsSamples map[string]c9sIfaceStatsSample\n\tnodes        map[string]*trackedNode\n\n\tnoShellMu sync.Mutex\n\t// noShell holds the pods whose device container has no shell; they are sampled with a\n\t// plain cat of /proc/net/dev and report statistics without interface state.\n\tnoShell map[string]bool\n\n\tlistingsMu sync.Mutex\n\t// listings holds the clabwire interface listing per pod (namespace/pod).\n\tlistings map[string]*podInterfaceListing\n\n\tfirstRound bool\n}\n\nfunc (r *Runtime) pollInterfaces(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tscope eventScope,\n\topts interfacePollOptions,\n\teventSink chan<- clablabruntime.Event,\n) {\n\tif opts.interval <= 0 {\n\t\topts.interval = time.Second\n\t}\n\n\tpoller := newInterfacePoller(r, scope, opts, eventSink)\n\tpoller.round(ctx)\n\n\tticker := time.NewTicker(opts.interval)\n\tdefer ticker.Stop()\n\n\tfor {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-ctx.Done():\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\tcase <-ticker.C:\n\t\t\tpoller.round(ctx)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc newInterfacePoller(\n\tr *Runtime,\n\tscope eventScope,\n\topts interfacePollOptions,\n\teventSink chan<- clablabruntime.Event,\n) *interfacePoller {\n\treturn &interfacePoller{\n\t\tr:            r,\n\t\tscope:        scope,\n\t\topts:         opts,\n\t\tsink:         eventSink,\n\t\tstatsSamples: map[string]c9sIfaceStatsSample{},\n\t\tnodes:        map[string]*trackedNode{},\n\t\tnoShell:      map[string]bool{},\n\t\tlistings:     map[string]*podInterfaceListing{},\n\t\tfirstRound:   true,\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *interfacePoller) round(ctx context.Context) {\n\tdefer func() { p.firstRound = false }()\n\n\tstates, err := p.r.labStates(ctx, p.scope)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"failed to list C9s labs for interface events\", \"error\", err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\trunning := map[string]bool{}\n\tpods := map[string]bool{}\n\tvar targets []interfaceSampleTarget\n\tfor _, state := range states {\n\t\tfor _, node := range state.Nodes {\n\t\t\tif node.ContainerState != clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning || node.Pod == \"\" ||\n\t\t\t\tnode.Container == \"\" {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\trunning[c9sNodeKey(state.Namespace, state.Name, node.Name)] = true\n\t\t\tpods[state.Namespace+\"/\"+node.Pod] = true\n\t\t\ttargets = append(targets, interfaceSampleTarget{\n\t\t\t\tstate: state,\n\t\t\t\tnode:  node,\n\t\t\t\tpod: &corev1.Pod{ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{\n\t\t\t\t\tName:      node.Pod,\n\t\t\t\t\tNamespace: state.Namespace,\n\t\t\t\t}},\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, sample := range p.sampleAll(ctx, targets) {\n\t\tif ctx.Err() != nil {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tif sample.err != nil {\n\t\t\tlog.Debug(\"failed to sample C9s interfaces\",\n\t\t\t\t\"namespace\", sample.target.state.Namespace,\n\t\t\t\t\"lab\", sample.target.state.Name,\n\t\t\t\t\"node\", sample.target.node.Name,\n\t\t\t\t\"error\", sample.err,\n\t\t\t)\n\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tp.processSample(ctx, sample)\n\t}\n\n\tp.retireStoppedNodes(ctx, running)\n\tp.forgetListings(pods)\n}\n\n// retireStoppedNodes reports the interfaces of nodes that stopped running, or were removed, as\n// deleted: they are gone with the node's pod.\nfunc (p *interfacePoller) retireStoppedNodes(ctx context.Context, running map[string]bool) {\n\tfor key, tracked := range p.nodes {\n\t\tif running[key] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tfor _, name := range sortedInterfaceNames(tracked.ifaces) {\n\t\t\tp.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionDelete, tracked.ifaces[name], time.Now())\n\t\t\tp.forgetStats(tracked, name)\n\t\t}\n\t\tdelete(p.nodes, key)\n\t}\n}\n\n// forgetListings drops the interface listings of pods that are gone.\nfunc (p *interfacePoller) forgetListings(pods map[string]bool) {\n\tp.listingsMu.Lock()\n\tdefer p.listingsMu.Unlock()\n\n\tfor key := range p.listings {\n\t\tif !pods[key] {\n\t\t\tdelete(p.listings, key)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *interfacePoller) sampleAll(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\ttargets []interfaceSampleTarget,\n) []interfaceSample {\n\tsamples := make([]interfaceSample, len(targets))\n\n\tvar wg sync.WaitGroup\n\tsem := make(chan struct{}, interfaceSampleWorkers)\n\tfor idx := range targets {\n\t\twg.Add(1)\n\t\tsem <- struct{}{}\n\t\tgo func(idx int) {\n\t\t\tdefer wg.Done()\n\t\t\tdefer func() { <-sem }()\n\n\t\t\tsamples[idx] = p.sample(ctx, targets[idx])\n\t\t}(idx)\n\t}\n\twg.Wait()\n\n\treturn samples\n}\n\nfunc (p *interfacePoller) sample(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\ttarget interfaceSampleTarget,\n) interfaceSample {\n\tsample := interfaceSample{target: target}\n\tpodName := target.pod.Name\n\n\tp.noShellMu.Lock()\n\tnoShell := p.noShell[podName]\n\tp.noShellMu.Unlock()\n\n\tcommand := []string{\"sh\", \"-c\", interfaceSampleScript}\n\tif noShell {\n\t\tcommand = []string{\"cat\", \"/proc/net/dev\"}\n\t}\n\n\tstdout, stderr, rc, err := p.r.execInPod(ctx, target.pod, target.node.Container, command)\n\tif !noShell && commandNotExecutable(rc, err) {\n\t\tp.noShellMu.Lock()\n\t\tp.noShell[podName] = true\n\t\tp.noShellMu.Unlock()\n\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"C9s device container has no shell; reporting interface statistics only\",\n\t\t\t\"namespace\", target.state.Namespace,\n\t\t\t\"lab\", target.state.Name,\n\t\t\t\"node\", target.node.Name,\n\t\t)\n\n\t\tstdout, stderr, rc, err = p.r.execInPod(ctx, target.pod, target.node.Container,\n\t\t\t[]string{\"cat\", \"/proc/net/dev\"})\n\t}\n\n\tsample.timestamp = time.Now()\n\tswitch {\n\tcase err != nil:\n\t\tsample.err = err\n\tcase rc != 0:\n\t\tsample.err = fmt.Errorf(\"exit code %d: %s\", rc, strings.TrimSpace(string(stderr)))\n\tdefault:\n\t\tsample.stats, sample.ifaces, sample.hasStates, sample.err = parseInterfaceSample(stdout)\n\t}\n\tif sample.err != nil {\n\t\treturn sample\n\t}\n\n\tsample.links, sample.err = p.nodeLinks(ctx, target, sampledInterfaceNames(sample))\n\n\treturn sample\n}\n\n// sampledInterfaceNames lists the interface names a sample saw, sorted and comma-joined.\nfunc sampledInterfaceNames(sample interfaceSample) string {\n\tnames := make([]string, 0, len(sample.stats)+len(sample.ifaces))\n\tseen := map[string]bool{}\n\tfor _, iface := range sample.ifaces {\n\t\tif !seen[iface.Name] {\n\t\t\tseen[iface.Name] = true\n\t\t\tnames = append(names, iface.Name)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor _, stat := range sample.stats {\n\t\tif !seen[stat.Name] {\n\t\t\tseen[stat.Name] = true\n\t\t\tnames = append(names, stat.Name)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(names)\n\n\treturn strings.Join(names, \",\")\n}\n\n// nodeLinks returns the lab link interfaces of a node from its pod's clabwire listing. A pod is\n// listed once, and again when its interfaces change (a pod gets its link interfaces as clabwire\n// wires them).\nfunc (p *interfacePoller) nodeLinks(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\ttarget interfaceSampleTarget,\n\tnames string,\n) ([]clabwireInterface, error) {\n\tkey := target.pod.Namespace + \"/\" + target.pod.Name\n\n\tp.listingsMu.Lock()\n\tlisting := p.listings[key]\n\tp.listingsMu.Unlock()\n\n\tif listing == nil || listing.names != names {\n\t\tentries, err := p.r.listPodInterfaces(ctx, target.pod.Namespace, target.pod.Name)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tlisting = &podInterfaceListing{\n\t\t\tnames:  names,\n\t\t\tbyNode: map[string][]clabwireInterface{},\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, entry := range entries {\n\t\t\tlisting.byNode[entry.Node] = append(listing.byNode[entry.Node], entry)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tp.listingsMu.Lock()\n\t\tp.listings[key] = listing\n\t\tp.listingsMu.Unlock()\n\t}\n\n\treturn listing.byNode[target.node.Name], nil\n}\n\n// commandNotExecutable reports an exec that failed because the command does not exist in the\n// container.\nfunc commandNotExecutable(rc int, err error) bool {\n\tif rc == exitCommandNotExecutable || rc == exitCommandNotFound {\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\n\treturn err != nil && strings.Contains(err.Error(), \"executable file not found\")\n}\n\n// reportedInterfaces are the interfaces reported for a node, by name, with the alias the\n// topology gave them: its lab link interfaces, the management interface and loopback.\nfunc reportedInterfaces(links []clabwireInterface) map[string]string {\n\treported := map[string]string{\n\t\tloopbackInterface:   \"\",\n\t\tmanagementInterface: \"\",\n\t}\n\tfor _, link := range links {\n\t\treported[link.Interface] = link.Alias\n\t}\n\n\treturn reported\n}\n\n// interfaceEventData describes an interface the way the local runtimes' netlink events do: the\n// alias is the topology's name for the interface (an alias clabernetes set for its own use is\n// not reported), the operational state uses netlink's names, lab link and management\n// interfaces are veth pairs, loopback a device, and loopback has no hardware address.\nfunc interfaceEventData(iface c9sIfaceState, alias string) clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData {\n\tif alias == \"\" && !strings.HasPrefix(iface.Alias, clabernetesAliasPrefix) {\n\t\talias = iface.Alias\n\t}\n\n\tmac := iface.MAC\n\tif mac == zeroMAC {\n\t\tmac = \"\"\n\t}\n\n\tlinkType := interfaceTypeVeth\n\tif iface.Name == loopbackInterface {\n\t\tlinkType = interfaceTypeDevice\n\t}\n\n\treturn clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData{\n\t\tName:      iface.Name,\n\t\tAlias:     alias,\n\t\tIndex:     iface.Index,\n\t\tMTU:       iface.MTU,\n\t\tMAC:       mac,\n\t\tOperState: netlinkOperState(iface.OperState),\n\t\tType:      linkType,\n\t}\n}\n\n// netlinkOperState names an operational state from sysfs (RFC 2863, as in\n// /sys/class/net/<if>/operstate) the way netlink, and so the local runtimes' events, name it.\nfunc netlinkOperState(operState string) string {\n\tswitch operState {\n\tcase \"notpresent\":\n\t\treturn \"not-present\"\n\tcase \"lowerlayerdown\":\n\t\treturn \"lower-layer-down\"\n\tcase \"\":\n\t\treturn \"unknown\"\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn operState\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *interfacePoller) processSample(ctx context.Context, sample interfaceSample) {\n\tstate := sample.target.state\n\tnode := sample.target.node\n\tkey := c9sNodeKey(state.Namespace, state.Name, node.Name)\n\n\ttracked, known := p.nodes[key]\n\tif !known {\n\t\ttracked = &trackedNode{ifaces: map[string]clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData{}}\n\t\tp.nodes[key] = tracked\n\t}\n\ttracked.lab = state\n\ttracked.node = node\n\n\treported := reportedInterfaces(sample.links)\n\n\tif sample.hasStates {\n\t\tp.processStates(ctx, tracked, reported, sample)\n\t}\n\n\tif !p.opts.includeStats {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tfor _, stat := range sample.stats {\n\t\talias, ok := reported[stat.Name]\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tstatsKey := c9sIfaceStatsKey(state.Namespace, state.Name, node.Name, stat.Name)\n\t\tcurrent := c9sIfaceStatsSample{Stats: stat, Timestamp: sample.timestamp}\n\t\tif previous, ok := p.statsSamples[statsKey]; ok {\n\t\t\tdata, ok := tracked.ifaces[stat.Name]\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\tdata = interfaceEventData(c9sIfaceState{Name: stat.Name}, alias)\n\t\t\t\tdata.OperState = \"\"\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tdata.Stats = c9sIfaceStatsData(previous, current)\n\t\t\tp.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionStats, data, current.Timestamp)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tp.statsSamples[statsKey] = current\n\t}\n}\n\n// processStates reports the interfaces that appeared (snapshot in the first round with\n// --initial-state, create later), changed (update) or disappeared (delete) since the last\n// sample, like the netlink events of the local runtimes.\nfunc (p *interfacePoller) processStates(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\ttracked *trackedNode,\n\treported map[string]string,\n\tsample interfaceSample,\n) {\n\tpresent := map[string]bool{}\n\tfor _, iface := range sample.ifaces {\n\t\talias, ok := reported[iface.Name]\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tdata := interfaceEventData(iface, alias)\n\t\tpresent[iface.Name] = true\n\t\tprevious, seen := tracked.ifaces[iface.Name]\n\t\ttracked.ifaces[iface.Name] = data\n\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase seen && previous == data:\n\t\tcase !seen && p.firstRound:\n\t\t\t// Interfaces that exist when the stream starts are only reported with\n\t\t\t// --initial-state; later changes are always reported.\n\t\t\tif p.opts.includeInitialState {\n\t\t\t\tp.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionSnapshot, data, sample.timestamp)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tcase !seen:\n\t\t\tp.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionCreate, data, sample.timestamp)\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tp.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionUpdate, data, sample.timestamp)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, name := range sortedInterfaceNames(tracked.ifaces) {\n\t\tif present[name] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tp.emit(ctx, tracked, interfaceActionDelete, tracked.ifaces[name], sample.timestamp)\n\t\tp.forgetStats(tracked, name)\n\t\tdelete(tracked.ifaces, name)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc sortedInterfaceNames(ifaces map[string]clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData) []string {\n\tnames := make([]string, 0, len(ifaces))\n\tfor name := range ifaces {\n\t\tnames = append(names, name)\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(names)\n\n\treturn names\n}\n\nfunc (p *interfacePoller) forgetStats(tracked *trackedNode, ifName string) {\n\tdelete(p.statsSamples,\n\t\tc9sIfaceStatsKey(tracked.lab.Namespace, tracked.lab.Name, tracked.node.Name, ifName))\n}\n\nfunc (p *interfacePoller) emit(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\ttracked *trackedNode,\n\taction string,\n\tdata clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData,\n\ttimestamp time.Time,\n) {\n\tp.r.sendEvent(ctx, p.sink, c9sInterfaceEvent(tracked, action, data, timestamp))\n}\n\n// c9sInterfaceEvent is an interface event of a node. The actor is the node, as for its container\n// events. The interface itself is in Interface; the events command reports it with the\n// attributes of the local runtimes' interface events.\nfunc c9sInterfaceEvent(\n\ttracked *trackedNode,\n\taction string,\n\tdata clablabruntime.InterfaceEventData,\n\ttimestamp time.Time,\n) clablabruntime.Event {\n\tkey := c9sNodeKey(tracked.lab.Namespace, tracked.lab.Name, tracked.node.Name)\n\n\tattributes := map[string]string{\n\t\t\"namespace\": tracked.lab.Namespace,\n\t\t\"lab\":       tracked.lab.Name,\n\t\t\"node\":      tracked.node.Name,\n\t\t\"origin\":    clabernetesAppValue,\n\t}\n\tif tracked.node.Pod != \"\" {\n\t\tattributes[\"pod\"] = tracked.node.Pod\n\t}\n\n\tnode := tracked.node\n\n\treturn clablabruntime.Event{\n\t\tTimestamp:   timestamp,\n\t\tType:        clablabruntime.EventTypeInterface,\n\t\tAction:      action,\n\t\tActorID:     key,\n\t\tActorName:   fmt.Sprintf(\"%s-%s\", tracked.lab.Name, tracked.node.Name),\n\t\tActorFullID: key,\n\t\tAttributes:  attributes,\n\t\tLab:         tracked.lab,\n\t\tNode:        &node,\n\t\tInterface:   &data,\n\t}\n}\n\n// c9sIfaceStatsData computes the counters and rates of a stats event from two samples.\nfunc c9sIfaceStatsData(previous, current c9sIfaceStatsSample) *clablabruntime.InterfaceStats {\n\tinterval := current.Timestamp.Sub(previous.Timestamp)\n\tif interval <= 0 {\n\t\tinterval = time.Second\n\t}\n\n\tseconds := interval.Seconds()\n\tstat := current.Stats\n\n\treturn &clablabruntime.InterfaceStats{\n\t\tRxBytes:   stat.RxBytes,\n\t\tTxBytes:   stat.TxBytes,\n\t\tRxPackets: stat.RxPackets,\n\t\tTxPackets: stat.TxPackets,\n\t\tRxBps:     float64(counterDelta(stat.RxBytes, previous.Stats.RxBytes)*8) / seconds,\n\t\tTxBps:     float64(counterDelta(stat.TxBytes, previous.Stats.TxBytes)*8) / seconds,\n\t\tRxPps:     float64(counterDelta(stat.RxPackets, previous.Stats.RxPackets)) / seconds,\n\t\tTxPps:     float64(counterDelta(stat.TxPackets, previous.Stats.TxPackets)) / seconds,\n\t\tInterval:  interval,\n\t}\n}\n\n// parseInterfaceSample splits the output of interfaceSampleScript into the /proc/net/dev\n// counters and the sysfs interface states. hasStates is false for output without the sysfs\n// section, such as a plain cat of /proc/net/dev.\nfunc parseInterfaceSample(data []byte) ([]c9sIfaceStats, []c9sIfaceState, bool, error) {\n\ttext := string(data)\n\n\tprocPart, sysfsPart, hasStates := strings.Cut(text, interfaceSysfsMarker+\"\\n\")\n\tif !hasStates {\n\t\tprocPart, _, hasStates = strings.Cut(text, interfaceSysfsMarker)\n\t}\n\n\tstats, err := parseProcNetDev([]byte(procPart))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif !hasStates {\n\t\treturn stats, nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\n\treturn stats, parseSysfsInterfaces(sysfsPart), true, nil\n}\n\nfunc parseSysfsInterfaces(data string) []c9sIfaceState {\n\tlines := strings.Split(data, \"\\n\")\n\tstates := make([]c9sIfaceState, 0, len(lines))\n\n\tfor _, line := range lines {\n\t\tfields := strings.SplitN(line, \"\\t\", 7) //nolint:mnd\n\t\tif len(fields) < 5 || strings.TrimSpace(fields[0]) == \"\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tstate := c9sIfaceState{\n\t\t\tName:      strings.TrimSpace(fields[0]),\n\t\t\tMAC:       strings.TrimSpace(fields[3]),\n\t\t\tOperState: strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(fields[4])),\n\t\t}\n\t\tstate.Index, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(fields[1]))\n\t\tstate.MTU, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(fields[2]))\n\t\tif len(fields) > 5 {\n\t\t\tstate.Flags, _ = strconv.ParseUint(\n\t\t\t\tstrings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(fields[5]), \"0x\"), 16, 20: func (r *Runtime) StreamEvents(
21: 	ctx context.Context,
22: 	req clablabruntime.EventStreamRequest,
23: ) (<-chan clablabruntime.Event, <-chan error, error) {
24: 	r, connErr := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
25: 	if connErr != nil {
26: 		return nil, nil, connErr
27: 	}
28: 
29: 	scope, err := r.eventScopeFor(req)
30: 	if err != nil {
31: 		return nil, nil, err
32: 	}
33: 
34: 	events := make(chan clablabruntime.Event, 128)
35: 	errs := make(chan error, 4)
36: 	// changed carries the labs whose Topology, Nodes or pods changed; the container tracker
37: 	// reads them again and reports what changed for their nodes.
38: 	changed := make(chan labRef, 256)
39: 
40: 	go r.trackContainers(ctx, scope, req.IncludeInitialState, changed, events, errs)
41: 
42: 	// Interface state events are always reported, like the netlink-backed events of the local
43: 	// runtimes; statistics only on request. Both come from the same exec per node.
44: 	go r.pollInterfaces(ctx, scope, interfacePollOptions{
45: 		interval:            req.StatsInterval,
46: 		includeStats:        req.IncludeInterfaceStats,
47: 		includeInitialState: req.IncludeInitialState,
48: 	}, events)
49: 
50: 	go r.watchTopologies(ctx, scope, changed, events, errs)
51: 	go r.watchNodes(ctx, scope, changed, errs)
52: 	go r.watchPods(ctx, scope, changed, errs)
53: 
54: 	return events, errs, nil
55: }

With `-t` loaded, config's NodeType would be non-empty for srl. 53: func (r *Runtime) trackContainers(
54: 	ctx context.Context,

67: 	}
68: 	for _, state := range states {
69: 		tracker.observeLab(ctx, labRef{namespace: state.Namespace, lab: state.Name}, state,
70: 			&observeSeed{snapshot: includeInitialState})

73: 	pending := map[labRef]bool{}
74: 	timer := time.NewTimer(time.Hour)
75: 	timer.Stop()
76: 	defer timer.Stop()
77: 	armed := false
78: 	arm := func(delay time.Duration) {
79: 		if !armed {
80: 			timer.Reset(delay)
81: 			armed = true
82: 		}
83: 	}
84: 
85: 	for {
86: 		select {

88: 			return

154: 	}

161: 		for _, action := range containerRemovalActions(tracked) {

168: func (t *containerTracker) observeNode(
169: 	ctx context.Context,
170: 	ref labRef,

193: 				"origin": clablabruntime.EventOriginSnapshot,

200: 	for _, action := range containerTransitionActions(previous, next) {

205: // containerHealth is the health a running node reports: a node that was healthy and is not
206: // ready anymore in the same pod is unhealthy, as a container whose healthcheck starts failing.
207: func containerHealth(previous, next *trackedContainer, health string) string {
208: 	if next.state != clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning {
209: 		return ""
210: 	}
211: 	if health == "" {
212: 		health = clablabruntime.ContainerHealthStarting

224: // containerTransitionActions are the container event actions Docker reports when a container

236: // node reports health changes, like a container with a healthcheck.
237: func containerTransitionActions(previous, next *trackedContainer) []string {
238: 	const (
239: 		created = clablabruntime.ContainerStateCreated
240: 		running = clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning
241: 		exited  = clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited
242: 	)

244: 	var actions []string

248: 	}

250: 	switch {

256: 		case exited:

260: 		actions = append(actions, containerActionKill, containerActionStop, containerActionDie,
261: 			containerActionStart)
262: 	case previousState == running && next.state != running:
263: 		actions = append(actions, containerActionKill, containerActionStop, containerActionDie)
264: 	case previousState != running && next.state == running:
265: 		actions = append(actions, containerActionStart)
266: 	case previousState == created && next.state == exited:
267: 		actions = append(actions, containerActionStop)

269: 
270: 	if next.state != running {

272: 	}

285: // containerRemovalActions are the actions Docker reports when a container is removed: a running

288: 	if previous.state == clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning {

302: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateExited

304: 		return clablabruntime.ContainerStateRunning

323: // c9sContainerEvent is a container event of a node. The actor is the node, as for its interface
324: // events; its ID is the container_id inspect reports. Lab and Node let the events command
325: // describe the node with the attributes inspect and the Docker runtime report.
326: func c9sContainerEvent(
327: 	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
328: 	node clablabruntime.NodeState,
329: 	action string,
330: 	extra map[string]string,
331: ) clablabruntime.Event {

333: 	attributes := map[string]string{

335: 		"lab":                        state.Name,
336: 		"node":                       node.Name,
337: 		containerEventAttributeState: containerActionState(action, node.ContainerState),

339: 	if node.Pod != "" {

342: 	if action == containerActionKill {

347: 		attributes[k] = v
348: 	}
349: 
350: 	nodeCopy := node
351: 
352: 	return clablabruntime.Event{
353: 		Timestamp:   time.Now(),
354: 		Type:        clablabruntime.EventTypeContainer,
355: 		Action:      action,
356: 		ActorID:     key,
357: 		ActorName:   fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", state.Name, node.Name),
358: 		ActorFullID: key,

Reasoning
One subtle behavior in `containerTransitionActions`: `case previousState != running && next.state == running: actions = append(actions, containerActionStart)` — this catches `previousState == exited -> running` (restart), and also `previousState == ""`? No, previous==nil handled. What about previousState == exited and next.state == created? falls to default (no actions) — fine.

Edge: `previousState == exited && next.state == exited` — no actions. Fine.

`started` detection: actions last element == start. For a restart (running→running new pod), actions end with start, and health appended. If health is "healthy" and started → emits health_status: healthy. If health is "starting" and started → emits health_status: starting. Per robot test: health_status: healthy appended. OK.

Edge: if next.health == "starting" and started is false and previous != nil and previous.health != next.health — third check `next.health == starting && !started` returns actions (no health event) — correct, matches "starting only on start".

Wait, there's a subtle bug candidate: second check `if !started && previous != nil && previous.health == next.health { return actions }`. If `started` is false and previous.health != next.health and next.health is healthy → append health_status: healthy. Good. If started is true, skip this check, then third check: next.health == starting && !started → false, so append health_status: starting/healthy. Good.

But what if actions is nil (no state change) and previous == nil? previous==nil always yields create so actions non-nil. If no transition (same state, same pod), actions is nil, started=false, previous.health == next.health → return nil. If health changed from healthy to starting (same pod, same state) → containerHealth would have returned unhealthy (if previous healthy/starting→unhealthy when starting on same pod) or healthy. Health transitions emit health_status. OK.

Now, one thing: `containerHealth` returns unhealthy when a previously healthy node becomes not-ready in same pod. But it never transitions back from unhealthy to starting/healthy? If health == healthy it returns healthy — recovers. Good.

787: Interface Event Should Be Logged
788:     [Documentation]    An interface event with the action and, when given, one of the states.
789:     [Arguments]    ${path}    ${node}    ${ifname}    ${action}    @{states}
790:     ${contents} =    Get File    ${path}
791:     ${actor} =    Set Variable    ${lab-namespace}/${lab-name}/${node}
792:     ${found} =    Evaluate
793:     ...    any([e.get("action") == $action and e.get("actor_id") == $actor and e.get("attributes", {}).get("ifname") == $ifname and (not $states or e.get("attributes", {}).get("state") in $states) for e in map(json.loads, filter(str.strip, $contents.splitlines())) if e.get("type") == "interface"])
794:     ...    modules=json
795:     Should Be True    ${found}    no interface ${action} event ${states} for ${node}:${ifname}
796: 
797: Last Interface State Should Be
798:     [Arguments]    ${path}    ${node}    ${ifname}    ${state}
799:     ${contents} =    Get File    ${path}
800:     ${states} =    Interface States    ${contents}    ${node}
801:     Should Be Equal    ${states}[${ifname}]    ${state}
802: 
803: Container Actions
804:     [Arguments]    ${path}    ${node}
805:     ${contents} =    Get File    ${path}
806:     ${actor} =    Set Variable    ${lab-namespace}/${lab-name}/${node}
807:     ${actions} =    Evaluate
808:     ...    [e["action"] for e in map(json.loads, filter(str.strip, $contents.splitlines())) if e.get("type") == "container" and e.get("actor_id") == $actor]
809:     ...    modules=json
810:     RETURN    ${actions}
811: 
812: Container Actions Should Include In Order
813:     [Arguments]    ${path}    ${node}    @{expected}
814:     ${actions} =    Container Actions    ${path}    ${node}
815:     # the expected actions appear in this order, other actions may come between them
816:     ${in_order} =    Evaluate
817:     ...    re.search("\\n" + "\\n(?:.*\\n)*?".join([re.escape(a) for a in $expected]) + "\\n", "\\n" + "\\n".join($actions) + "\\n") is not None
818:     ...    modules=re
819:     Should Be True    ${in_order}    ${node} reported ${actions}, not ${expected} in this order
820:

/source/base/docs/cmd/deploy.md:
  Line 261: `c9s` is a lab runtime, not a per-node container runtime. When it is selected, containerlab renders the topology and creates a Clabernetes `Topology` custom resource. See [Containerlab runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) for details.

  Line 347: The `--no-topology-cr` flag applies to the [clabernetes runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) only. By default, deploy persists the rendered topology as a c9s `Topology` resource and the Clabernetes manager compiles it into the `Node`, `Link`, and `NodeProfile` resources. With this flag, containerlab skips the `Topology` resource and compiles the topology client-side, creating and reconciling those resources directly.

  Line 355: The `--emit-crs` flag applies to the [clabernetes runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) only. Instead of applying anything, deploy prints the Kubernetes manifests it would create to stdout as a multi-document YAML stream, so they can be saved, edited by hand, and applied with `kubectl`. The cluster is not contacted.

  Line 371: The `--image-pull-secret` flag applies to the [clabernetes runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) only. It sets the name of the image pull secret populated in the c9s `Topology` CR (`spec.imagePull.pullSecrets`), which the kubelet uses when pulling node images. The secret must exist in the lab namespace.

  Line 398: The `--no-persistence` flag applies to the [clabernetes runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) only. By default, deploy enables persistence on the c9s `Topology` CR (`spec.deployment.persistence.enabled`), backing every node's artifact volume with a PersistentVolumeClaim so saved device configuration survives pod replacement -- the same contract the lab directory provides with local runtimes. The node names follow `inspect` (`<lab>-<node>`), and the JSON fields and values (`veth`/`device`, netlink state names) are the same as with Docker. `eth0` and `lo` cannot be captured on c9s.


/source/head/docs/cmd/inspect/index.md:
  Line 13: With `--runtime c9s`, `inspect` reads Clabernetes `Topology` resources and their related kubernetes objects instead of local Docker containers. `inspect --all` lists c9s topologies across all namespaces, or in the `--namespace` override. The JSON output uses `<namespace>/<lab>/<node>` as `container_id` and adds the `namespace`, `pod`, `container`, `node_uid`, `exposed_ports` and `load_balancer_address` fields. See [Containerlab runtime](../../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#inspect) for details.

  Line 98: - [Clabernetes containerlab runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#events) - describes c9s events and how they map onto Docker events.

  Line 10: - **c9s**: the `clabwire` sidecar of each node's pod captures the packets; see the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#packet-capture).


/source/head/docs/cmd/destroy.md:
  Line 33: With `--runtime c9s`, `--cleanup` also deletes the lab's persistent node storage (the PersistentVolumeClaims holding saved device configuration) and then the lab namespace. A plain destroy keeps the claims, so the next deploy of the lab boots from the saved configuration. See [device state persistence](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#device-state-persistence).


/source/head/docs/cmd/redeploy.md:
  Line 114: The `--no-topology-cr` flag applies to the [clabernetes runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) only. It makes the deploy phase skip the c9s `Topology` resource and create the compiled `Node`, `Link`, and `NodeProfile` resources directly. See [`deploy --no-topology-cr`](deploy.md#no-topology-cr).

  Line 118: The `--image-pull-secret` flag applies to the [clabernetes runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) only. It sets the name of the image pull secret populated in the c9s `Topology` CR during the deploy phase. See [`deploy --image-pull-secret`](deploy.md#image-pull-secret).

  Line 122: The `--no-persistence` flag applies to the [clabernetes runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) only. It makes the deploy phase run the lab nodes on ephemeral storage instead of the default per-node persistent volumes. See [`deploy --no-persistence`](deploy.md#no-persistence).


/source/head/docs/cmd/save.md:
  Line 11: [Containerlab runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#save) for details.


/source/head/docs/cmd/deploy.md:
  Line 261: `c9s` is a lab runtime, not a per-node container runtime. When it is selected, containerlab renders the topology and creates a Clabernetes `Topology` custom resource. See [Containerlab runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) for details.

  Line 347: The `--no-topology-cr` flag applies to the [clabernetes runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) only. By default, deploy persists the rendered topology as a c9s `Topology` resource and the Clabernetes manager compiles it into the `Node`, `Link`, and `NodeProfile` resources. With this flag, containerlab skips the `Topology` resource and compiles the topology client-side, creating and reconciling those resources directly.

  Line 355: The `--emit-crs` flag applies to the [clabernetes runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) only. Instead of applying anything, deploy prints the Kubernetes manifests it would create to stdout as a multi-document YAML stream, so they can be saved, edited by hand, and applied with `kubectl`. The cluster is not contacted.

  Line 371: The `--image-pull-secret` flag applies to the [clabernetes runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) only. It sets the name of the image pull secret populated in the c9s `Topology` CR (`spec.imagePull.pullSecrets`), which the kubelet uses when pulling node images. The secret must exist in the lab namespace.

445: func (r *Runtime) Inspect(
446: 	ctx context.Context,
447: 	req clablabruntime.InspectRequest,
448: ) (*clablabruntime.LabState, error) {
449: 	r, connErr := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
450: 	if connErr != nil {
451: 		return nil, connErr
452: 	}
453: 
454: 	if req.Name == "" {
455: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("topology name is required")
456: 	}
457: 
458: 	namespace, err := r.namespaceForLab(req.Name, req.Namespace)
459: 	if err != nil {
460: 		return nil, err
461: 	}
462: 	obj, err := r.client.Resource(topologyGVR).Namespace(namespace).
463: 		Get(ctx, req.Name, metav1.GetOptions{})
464: 	if err != nil && !apierrors.IsNotFound(err) {
465: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to inspect clabernetes topology %s/%s: %w",
466: 			namespace, req.Name, err)
467: 	}
468: 
469: 	var state *clablabruntime.LabState

545: unchanged. Fields without a value, such as `pod` for a stopped node, are left
546: out. `--details` keeps printing the raw records.
547: 
548: The other fields mean what they mean for Docker and Podman, so clients can treat
549: c9s nodes like containers:
550: 
551: | Field | c9s value |
552: |---|---|
553: | `state` | `created` while the node's pod is scheduled and prepared, `running` once its device containers run, `exited` once the node is stopped (or its pod ends or is replaced) |
554: | `status` | `healthy` once the node is ready or its device containers are, `health: starting` while a running device boots, `Created`, `Exited` |
555: | `labPath`, `absLabPath` | the topology file the lab was deployed from (see below) |
556: | `name` | `<lab>-<node>`, the name events use as `actor_name` |
557: 
558: ### Topology file
559: 
560: A deploy records the absolute path of the topology file, on the machine that
561: deployed it, in the annotation `containerlab.dev/topo-file`:
562: 
563: - with a `Topology` resource, on the `Topology`; every deploy records the file
564:   it read
565: - with `--no-topology-cr`, on every `Node`. clabernetes copies a Node's
566:   annotations into its pod, so a Node keeps the file it was created from: a
567:   later deploy from another file does not change it and does not restart the
568:   node. Destroy and deploy again to record a new file.
569: 
570: `inspect` reports the recorded file as `labPath` and `absLabPath` (shortened
571: for the table, as for Docker), and events as `clab-topo-file`, so a client
572: matches a running lab to its file the same way for every runtime. The file is a
573: path on the deploying machine; a client on another machine cannot assume it
574: exists there.
575: 
576: A lab that containerlab did not deploy from a file, for example one applied from
577: `deploy --emit-crs` output with `kubectl` (the emitted manifests do not carry
578: the annotation), has no recorded file. It reports where its definition lives in
579: the cluster: `k8s://<namespace>/topologies/<lab>`, or
580: `k8s://<namespace>/labs/<lab>` without a `Topology` resource. With `-t`,
581: `inspect` reports the given file.
582: 
583: Useful kubernetes checks for the same state are:
584: 
585: ```bash
586: kubectl -n <namespace> get node.c9s.run,link.c9s.run,nodeprofile.c9s.run,deploy,pod,svc,cm,pvc \
587:   -l c9s.run/topologyOwner=<lab>
588: ```
589: 
590: ## Exec
591: 
592: `exec` runs the user command in the node's device container:
593: 
594: ```bash
595: containerlab --runtime c9s exec -t topo.clab.yml --cmd 'ip addr'
596: ```
597: 
598: Under the hood, containerlab:
599: 
600: 1. resolves the target nodes from the Clabernetes lab state
601: 2. finds the device pod for each node (grouped nodes share the primary node's pod)
602: 3. selects the node's application container from the Node status — for an
603:    SR-SIM chassis this is the active-preferred CPM component
604: 4. uses kubernetes pod exec directly into that container
605: 
606: /// note
607: The command executes in the actual device container. RBAC must allow
608: `pods/exec`, and the device pod must be running.
609: ///
610: 
611: `exec` does not check for a local Docker or Podman daemon; the outer host only
612: needs to reach the cluster.
613: 
614: If any selected command returns nonzero, or pod exec itself fails, the outer
615: `containerlab exec` also returns nonzero. Successful and failed results that
616: were received are still printed, so automation can use both the output and the
617: process exit status.
618: 
619: ## Logs
620: 
621: `logs` shows the log of a node's primary device container, the same container
622: `exec` uses:
623: 
624: ```bash
625: containerlab --runtime c9s logs -t topo.clab.yml -n srl1
626: containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps
627: ```
628: 
629: It reads the `pods/log` subresource of the node's pod, so RBAC must allow
630: `get` on `pods/log`. Kubernetes returns stdout and stderr as one stream. See
631: the [`logs` command](../../cmd/logs.md) for the flags.
632: 
633: ## Packet capture
634: 
635: [`containerlab capture`](../../cmd/capture.md) captures lab link interfaces of
636: one or more nodes into one pcapng stream. Each node's pod runs the `clabwire`
637: sidecar, which realized the node's links; containerlab execs its capture
638: command (`/clabernetes/manager node-runtime packet-capture`) in the sidecar.
639: No capture service runs in the cluster, and nothing is captured outside the
640: lab's planned link interfaces.
641: 
642: ```bash
643: # both ends of a link, for 30 seconds
644: containerlab -r c9s capture -t clos.clab.yml \
645:   --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 --duration 30s -w srl.pcapng
646: 
647: # live in Wireshark until Wireshark or Ctrl+C ends it
648: containerlab -r c9s capture --name clos --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - | wireshark -k -i -
649: 
650: # what can be captured, with the peer of each link
651: containerlab -r c9s capture --name clos --list
652: ```
653: 
654: How it works:
655: 
656: - containerlab locates each target node's pod and runs one `clabwire` capture
657:   per node, with `--nodeName`, every requested interface of that node,
658:   `--format pcapng` and `--stop-on-stdin-close`, with stdin attached.
659: - The streams are merged into one section: one Interface Description Block per
660:   target named `<node>:<interface>` (the node as the topology spells it),
661:   written before the first packet, and the packets of every target with their
662:   interface IDs remapped.
663: - Packets are written in timestamp order. Each node's stream arrives over its
664:   own exec stream, so the merged stream holds every packet for 250 ms and
